pages.title: Overview
pages.description: What the app does, and where to start.
pages.intro: Loan Debt Service Hub keeps your whole loan book in one place: every loan with its payment schedule, every property with its T12, rent roll and documents, the underwriting you approve, and the refinance it supports. Your data is saved on this computer, or in the shared database for your whole team. With Claude connected, the app reads each T12 a second time, writes the stories behind the numbers, suggests what to push, and answers your questions.

steps.text: **Look over the portfolio.** The app opens on the **Portfolio** tab: what needs your attention, the totals and every loan. See [Find your way around](get-around).
**Open a loan** to see its terms, its coverage and every payment. See [Open a loan](open-a-loan).
**Connect Claude** for the AI features: your Claude subscription, or an API key. See [Connect Claude](connect-claude).
**Underwrite a property** from its T12, then approve it. See [Upload a T12](upload-a-t12).

cards.title: Track every loan

cards.title: Decide on a refinance

cards.title: See what’s coming due

cards.title: Keep each property’s files
cards.text: T12s, rent rolls and agreements in the property’s own folder. A T12 is checked before anything uses it.

pages.title: Check each property’s coverage
pages.description: See which properties clear your DSCR, debt-yield and LTV targets, and add the NOI of the ones without one.
pages.intro: The Portfolio page measures the whole book, and every property in it, against your targets: a minimum DSCR, a minimum debt yield and a maximum LTV. Check it to find the properties that miss a target, the ones with no NOI yet, and the ones paying well above today’s market rate.

callouts.text: The targets (1.25×, 8% …) are set in Settings. See [Set the portfolio targets](set-portfolio-targets).

steps.text: On the **Portfolio** tab, read **Portfolio DSCR** and **Portfolio Debt Yield**, under the heading. Each says how the whole book stands against your target.

marks.label: Portfolio DSCR
marks.text: Total NOI ÷ total yearly loan payments, against your minimum DSCR.

marks.label: Portfolio Debt Yield
marks.text: Total NOI ÷ total balance, against your minimum debt yield.

steps.text: Look at **Coverage vs targets**, under the tiles. Each bar is the portfolio’s figure and the thin dark line is your target: green clears it, amber is close, red is off. Under the bars, every property that is off a target is named.

marks.label: Portfolio DSCR
marks.text: Against your minimum DSCR.

marks.label: Portfolio LTV
marks.text: Against your maximum LTV: lower is better here.

marks.label: Off a target
marks.text: Every property that misses a target or has no NOI yet.

callouts.text: A property with no NOI yet counts as $0 NOI, so its debt pulls the portfolio’s DSCR and debt yield down. The tiles say how many such properties there are.

steps.text: Scroll down to **Coverage**. Each row is one property, worst DSCR first; a senior loan and its mezzanine count as one. Properties with no NOI yet are at the bottom.

marks.label: DSCR
marks.text: NOI ÷ yearly loan payments. Green clears the target, amber is close, red is off.

marks.label: Gap
marks.text: The property’s rate today minus the market’s. Green: more than 0.25% above market.

marks.label: Off target
marks.text: Misses at least one target.

marks.label: Needs T12/NOI
marks.text: No NOI yet.

steps.text: Read the tag at the end of each row: **clears** meets all three targets, **off target** misses at least one, and **needs T12/NOI** has no NOI yet.
Compare **Current** with **Market**: the rate the property pays now against what the same loan would cost today. A green **Gap** is worth a look at a refinance.

callouts.text: The picture shows the first rows; the table lists every property.

steps.text: Click **Add NOI** on a property marked needs T12/NOI.

Type the property’s yearly NOI in **Property annual NOI**, from its operating statement. Change **Cap rate** only if you have a better figure than the default for its type; it gives the value, and so the LTV.

marks.label: Property annual NOI
marks.text: The yearly NOI, in dollars. It must be more than $0.

marks.label: Cap rate
marks.text: Filled in by property type. Value = NOI ÷ cap rate.

marks.label: Continue
marks.text: Saves the NOI and the cap rate.

steps.text: Click **Continue**. The row shows its DSCR, debt yield and LTV, and every total on the page counts it.

callouts.text: The property’s T12 gives a better NOI, and it is the only one a refinance uses. See [Upload a T12](upload-a-t12). (The NOI in the picture is made up and was not saved.)

steps.text: Click **Refi path** on the property’s row. The refinance opens for that property, all its loans together.

marks.label: Refinance Analysis
marks.text: The refinance for that property. Without a T12 it says “No T12 yet”.

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Back to the Portfolio page.

pages.title: Add a loan
pages.description: Put a loan in the book from its terms. The app works out the rest.
pages.intro: **Add Loan** opens an empty loan form. You type the terms from the loan papers; the app works out the balance, the payments, the debt service and the whole schedule from them. A new property name makes a new property, so a loan and its property can be added in one go.

sections.title: Fill in the loan
sections.text: Fields with a red * are required. Leave out what you don’t have.

pages.description: Flag a loan whose terms are no longer right, and say where a loan stands.
pages.intro: When a loan’s terms are no longer right — say it was refinanced and the new loan’s papers haven’t come — mark it out of date. Its figures stay as they are, but every place that shows them warns you. A loan’s status says where it stands: Active, Matured, Extended, Extension undecided or Paid off.

sections.title: How Claude chooses
sections.text: Claude works from four sources, and only four: the T12 (the source of truth), the rent roll, the loan agreement and the property details (units, address). It searches the web for the surroundings: market rents and rent growth, or the weather or an event in a given month. Every push raises the NOI on every version, never pulls a lever a story in the underwriting already pulls, and lists what Claude checked; one it couldn’t confirm is never shown. The “Claude didn’t have” note shows only when one of the four sources is missing.

callouts.text: Claude works out who pays the utilities from the T12 itself. A utilities line big enough for the whole property means the owner pays, in the rent, so Claude never suggests billing the residents for them. A line only big enough for the common areas means the residents pay their own.
Some vacancy is natural, so there is no push toward 100% occupancy. Rent growth at the market’s usual rate is measured on top of the rent the underwriting already counts.

pages.title: Run a refinance
pages.description: Open a loan’s refinance, check where today’s loan stands, and read the verdict: can you refinance, and should you?
pages.intro: The refinance answers two questions about a loan: can the property support a new loan the size of what you owe, and is it worth doing? It is worked out live from the property’s T12 (or its approved underwriting) and today’s rates. Nothing about the loan changes until you save something.
before: The property’s T12, uploaded in Underwriting — see [Upload a T12](upload-a-t12). A refinance is never sized on a typed NOI.

steps.text: Open the loan’s page: click its property on the **Portfolio** tab, or pick it under **Specific Property**. See [Open a loan](open-a-loan).
Click **Refi Calculator** at the top of the loan’s page. The refinance opens in its place.

marks.label: Refi Calculator
marks.text: Opens the refinance for the loan on this page.

steps.text: Read **Current Loan**: what you owe, the rate, the monthly payment and when the loan matures. A hybrid loan also says when its rate resets and what the payment becomes.

marks.label: Current Loan

marks.label: Rate reset

steps.text: Scroll to the colored box under **What to push**. Its first line is the answer; the line at the bottom says what to do.

steps.text: Read **Can you?**. When the answer is yes, **Should you?** under it says whether it is worth doing: the interest the new rate saves, against the early-payoff penalty.

callouts.text: The answer is one of four: **Refinance**; **Your decision**, when only the cash out makes it worth it; **Don’t refinance**; or **Act before** a date **— pay down** an amount, when the rate resets or the loan ends within 12 months and the property can’t support what you owe.
