Pick the preset in **Lender preset**. The limits fill in from it, and what the property supports is worked out again.

marks.label: Lender preset
marks.text: Pick a lender, or “None — type the limits”.

marks.label: Its name
marks.text: The preset in use.

marks.label: The limits
marks.text: Filled from the preset.

marks.label: What the property supports
marks.text: On the preset’s limits.

steps.text: Check **Proposed rate** above it. A rate type the lender doesn’t allow is greyed, and clicking it says why instead of switching.

marks.label: Fixed
marks.text: Allowed.

marks.label: Floating (greyed)
marks.text: Not allowed by this preset. Clicking it shows “Example Agency (made-up): no floating”.

marks.label: Hybrid
marks.text: Allowed.

callouts.text: For an extension, pick today’s lender’s preset in the extension’s own limits. It also fills in the penalty that lender usually asks. See [Extend with today’s lender](extend-with-your-lender).
Type over a limit to change it for this deal only. The preset’s name then says “(changed here)”.

next.text: Type the rest of the lender’s quote.
Every box in the presets window.

pages.title: Plan what to push for a refinance
pages.description: Pick the amount the new loan must cover, tick what you would push, and see whether the NOI gets there.
pages.intro: **What to push — what it would get you** is your plan, not the lender’s. Pick the amount the new loan has to cover, tick Claude’s pushes and your own levers, and see whether the NOI they add covers it. The coverage, the verdict and the proposed loan follow what you tick.
before: The property’s underwriting approved, with Claude’s **What to push** — see [See what you can still push](use-what-to-push). Your own levers work without it.

steps.text: Open the property’s refinance and pick the **NOI basis** in **Coverage & value**. Each push counts on that basis. See [Run a refinance](run-a-refinance).
Scroll to **What to push — what it would get you**. Under **The amount to cover**, click what the new loan has to cover.

marks.label: Today’s payoff
marks.text: What you owe today plus the early-payoff penalty. The starting choice.

marks.label: No penalty — the last 12 months
marks.text: What you will owe 12 months before maturity, when there is no penalty.

marks.label: At maturity
marks.text: What you will owe when the loan matures. Picked here.

marks.label: The NOI you need
marks.text: The NOI that covers that amount, and how much more it is than today’s.

steps.text: Read the line under the buttons: the NOI that covers that amount at the proposed rate and the lender’s limits, and how far today’s NOI is from it.
Tick a push in the list. What it adds on your basis goes into the NOI.
To count something of your own, type its name and the dollars it adds a year under **Add your own lever**, then click **Add**. It is added ticked.

marks.label: Added to the NOI
marks.text: Everything ticked, on this basis.

marks.label: Covered — or still missing
marks.text: Whether the NOI now covers the amount.

marks.label: A push, ticked
marks.text: Claude’s, from What to push in Underwriting.

marks.label: Your lever
marks.text: Marked “yours”; × removes it.

steps.text: Read the line under the amount again: **covered**, with what is to spare, or how much NOI is **still missing**.

callouts.text: Your ticks, your levers and the amount to cover are kept with this refinance for the whole team.

steps.text: Click another **NOI basis** in **Coverage & value**. The same push counts its effect on that basis: it is worth less on an underwriting that already counts part of it.

marks.label: Its effect on each basis
marks.text: First on the basis picked (now In-place T12), then in-place, Safe and Aggressive.

marks.label: Added to the NOI
marks.text: Follows the basis.

next.text: Where the pushes come from, and what Claude checked.
Set the rate and the lender’s limits the NOI is measured at.
Every part of What to push, named.

pages.title: Extend with today’s lender
pages.description: Judge an extension with today’s lender, set its terms, and save it on today’s loan.
pages.intro: Instead of a new loan, today’s lender may keep the loan on new terms, usually after a pay-down so it fits the lender’s limits. The refinance judges the extension by the same rule as a new loan: can you, and should you? Saving it changes today’s loan, and you can undo it.

callouts.text: One loan extends the same way however many properties it covers: it is sized on all of them. For several loans together (a senior + mezz, or a portfolio), see [Extend several loans together](refinance-together#extend-several-loans-together).

before: Today’s lender’s quote: the rate, its limits, the penalty and the fee it asks.

steps.text: Open the loan’s refinance. See [Run a refinance](run-a-refinance).
Under **What kind of deal?**, click **Extend with today’s lender**. The verdict, the limits and the schedule below now judge the extension. **New loan** switches back, and each keeps its own figures.
In the verdict box, under **The extension’s rate**, pick the **Index** and type today’s lender’s **Spread (bps)**.
In the limits table under it, type today’s lender’s own limits, and untick **Lender uses** on any it doesn’t use. Here 1.11× amortizing and 1.35× interest-only (made-up).

marks.label: Amortizing coverage
marks.text: Today’s lender’s DSCR.

marks.label: Interest-only coverage
marks.text: Its coverage on the interest-only payment.

marks.label: Lender uses
marks.text: Untick a limit it doesn’t use.

marks.label: What today’s lender allows
marks.text: The smallest of the limits it uses.

callouts.text: If the group has today’s lender’s preset, pick it in **Lender preset** there instead. It fills in the limits and the penalty that lender usually asks.

steps.text: Scroll to **The extension’s terms**. Set **Today’s terms end on**, **Months on the new terms**, **Interest-only** and the amortization after it.
Pick what this lender asks in **Early-payoff penalty — this lender asks**, and set the **Extension fee**. Until you pick, the penalty is assumed to be on the pay-down only.

marks.label: Early-payoff penalty
marks.text: The full penalty, on the pay-down only, a part, or none.

marks.label: Extension fee
marks.text: In % of the extended amount, or dollars.

marks.label: Pay-down needed
marks.text: So the loan fits the lender’s limits.

marks.label: Cash needed
marks.text: Pay-down + penalty + fee.

marks.label: Assumed
marks.text: Confirm the penalty with the lender.

steps.text: Scroll back up to the verdict box. **Can you?** gives the pay-down the extension needs, and the last line says what to do and the cash it takes.

marks.label: The answer
marks.text: Here: Extend, with a pay-down.

marks.label: The pay-down
marks.text: What you will owe less what the lender’s limits allow.

marks.label: Should you?
marks.text: Yes here: the rate resets within 12 months.

marks.label: Bottom line
marks.text: What to do, with the cash it takes.

steps.text: Click **Save the extension** at the top. A box lists what will change.

marks.label: Save the extension?
marks.text: It asks first.

marks.label: What happens
marks.text: The new terms, the pay-down, the penalty, the new maturity, the status and the cash needed.

marks.label: Save the extension
marks.text: Saves it.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Nothing changes.

steps.text: Click **Save the extension** in the box. Today’s loan stays the same record: from the date its terms end it has the new rate and term, the pay-down becomes a principal payment, and its status becomes Extended. Every changed field goes into the loan’s history.

callouts.text: **Save the extension** shows only when the answer is to extend. **Not yet** means nothing ends or resets within 12 months, so you decide closer to the date. **Don’t extend now** means the lower rate doesn’t pay for the penalty.

steps.text: Open the loan’s refinance again. It shows the saved extension.

marks.label: Extended with today’s lender
marks.text: The extension is saved on today’s loan.

marks.label: Saved
marks.text: When, and by whom. The loan’s own page has the extension too.

marks.label: What was saved
marks.text: The new terms, the pay-down, the new maturity and the cash it took.

marks.label: Undo the extension
marks.text: Puts today’s loan back as it was before.

marks.label: Change history
marks.text: The extension and every change before it.

steps.text: Click **Undo the extension**.

marks.label: Undo the extension?
marks.text: It asks first.

marks.label: What happens
marks.text: The loan goes back to its terms before the extension; the pay-down comes off the schedule; the history keeps both.

marks.label: Undo the extension
marks.text: Does it.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Keeps the extension.

steps.text: Click **Undo the extension** in the box. The rate, the maturity, the status and the schedule are put back, and the undo is in the history too.

next.text: Every box of the extension, named.
Set what the payment does at the reset.

pages.title: Refinance several loans together
pages.description: Refinance a senior and a mezzanine loan as one package, put several properties under one new loan, or extend each loan with its own lender.
pages.intro: Loans that depend on one another are refinanced together: a property’s senior and mezzanine loans, or several properties under one new loan. The refinance works the same way, on the package’s total NOI and everything it owes. Or keep today’s lenders: each loan is extended with its own lender, on its own terms.
before: A T12 for every property in the package — see [Upload a T12](upload-a-t12). Nothing is sized until each one has its T12.

sections.title: A senior and a mezzanine loan

steps.text: Click **Specific Property** and pick the property’s combined entry: its name followed by **senior + mezz**.
Click **Refi Calculator**. **Current debt** lists every loan on the property; one new loan pays them all off.

marks.label: The loans
marks.text: Here a senior and a mezzanine loan.

marks.label: Payoff balance
marks.text: Each loan at its own balance, added up.

marks.label: Current rate
marks.text: Weighted by what is owed on each.

sections.title: Several properties under one new loan

steps.text: On the **Portfolio** tab, click **Create a portfolio…** above the Coverage table.
Tick each property the new loan will secure. Each row shows what is owed and the NOI its refinance would use; the line under the list adds them up.

marks.label: Tick a property
marks.text: Each one the new loan will secure.

marks.label: Owes · NOI
marks.text: What is owed, and the NOI its refinance would use.

marks.label: The package
marks.text: The loans to pay off, what is owed and the NOI, together.

marks.label: Create the portfolio
marks.text: Needs at least two properties and one loan to pay off.

steps.text: Click **Create the portfolio**. The refinance opens for the whole package; nothing changes until you save.
In **NOI by property**, pick each property’s basis: **In-place T12**, or **Safe** or **Aggressive** once its underwriting is approved. The total, and everything below it, follows.

marks.label: Its basis
marks.text: The NOI this property counts with.

marks.label: NOI
marks.text: Its NOI on that basis.

marks.label: Total
marks.text: What the package is sized on.

steps.text: Read the verdict for the whole package. **Save as a loan** puts one new loan on all of the properties and pays off every loan on them. See [Save the refinance as a loan](save-the-refinance).

callouts.text: A ticked property with no T12 stops the package: the screen says **No T12 yet** and offers to upload it in Underwriting. A typed NOI never counts for a refinance.
**What to push** lists each property’s pushes under its name; tick them to see what the package could carry. See [Plan what to push for a refinance](plan-what-to-push).

sections.title: Extend several loans together
sections.text: Instead of one new loan, each loan stays with today’s lender, on new terms. Here K2 Sweetwater’s senior and mezzanine loans, which both mature within 12 months (with a made-up T12).

steps.text: Open the package’s refinance: the property’s **senior + mezz** entry, or **Create a portfolio…**, then **Refi Calculator**.

Under **What kind of deal?**, click **Extend with today’s lenders**. The verdict lists every loan: what you’ll owe when its terms end, what its lender allows, its pay-down, and whether to extend it now.

marks.label: The mezzanine
marks.text: Sized behind its senior.

marks.label: Its pay-down
marks.text: What it owes less what fits behind the senior.

marks.label: In all
marks.text: The pay-downs of the loans to extend now.

marks.label: Cash needed
marks.text: Pay-downs + penalties + fees.

steps.text: Scroll to each loan’s card and enter its lender’s quote: the **Spread (bps)**, the months, the penalty and the fee. A mezzanine is sized on the limits for the two loans together, less its senior’s extended amount.

marks.label: Behind its senior
marks.text: The senior’s extended amount comes first.

marks.label: Each limit
marks.text: What it leaves for the mezzanine; the smallest binds.

steps.text: Click **Save the extensions** at the top. Each loan stays its own record: from the date its terms end it has the new rate and term, its pay-down is recorded on its own schedule, and its status becomes Extended. **Undo** puts them all back.

callouts.text: The limits table applies to each loan. A loan that shouldn’t be extended now (**Not yet**, or **Don’t extend now**) is left as it is when you save the others.

next.text: Add a loan that already covers several properties.
Every part of a package refinance, named.

pages.title: Save the refinance as a loan
pages.description: Make the proposed loan a loan in your book, and mark today’s loan paid off.
pages.intro: When the answer is **Refinance**, **Your decision** or a pay-down, and the proposed loan matches your lender’s terms, save it. The new loan joins your book, and today’s loan is marked Paid off (refinanced) and leaves every total.
before: A proposed loan on the refinance — see [Set the proposed loan’s rate and amount](set-the-proposed-loan).

steps.text: Open the loan’s refinance and check the proposed loan: its rate, its amount and its terms. Here The Mews at Princeton, with the lender’s spread typed as 0 (made-up).
Click **Save as a loan** at the top. With a pay-down it reads **Save as a loan — pay in $X**; with **Your decision**, **Save as a loan — Refinance now**.

marks.label: Save as a loan
marks.text: Shown only when there is a loan to propose.

steps.text: Read **Save the refinance?**: the new loan, the loan it pays off, and any cash you pay in.

marks.label: Save the refinance?
marks.text: It asks first.

marks.label: What happens
marks.text: The new loan, the old loan(s) paid off, and any cash paid in.

marks.label: Save the refinance
marks.text: Does it.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Nothing changes.

steps.text: Click **Save the refinance**. The new loan is added with today’s date and opens on its own page. Today’s loan becomes Paid off (refinanced) and leaves every total; a pay-down is recorded on the new loan.

callouts.text: For a package, the one new loan secures every property in it, and every loan on them is paid off.

steps.text: On the **Portfolio** tab, scroll down to **Removed & paid-off loans**. Today’s loan is listed there as **Paid off (refinanced)**.

marks.label: Removed & paid-off loans
marks.text: Loans out of every total, tile and the calendar.

marks.label: Today’s loan
marks.text: Paid off (refinanced), with the date.

marks.label: Restore
marks.text: Brings it back into every total.

steps.text: To go back on the refinance, click **Restore** on today’s loan and remove the new loan. See [Bring back a removed loan or property](bring-back-removed) and [Remove a loan](remove-a-loan).

next.text: Read the new loan’s page.
See the property’s coverage with the new loan.

pages.title: Add a document
pages.description: Save a T12, a rent roll, a loan agreement or any other file to a property.
pages.intro: Every property keeps its files in its own folder. Add them on the property’s page: they stay with the property, and the assistant reads them when you talk about it, so you never upload a file twice.

steps.text: Open the property’s page: click **Specific Property** under the tabs and pick the property. **Documents** is near the bottom of the page.
Pick what you are adding in **What you are adding**, or leave **Detect automatically** to let the app look at what is in the file.

marks.label: Detect automatically
marks.text: The app reads the file and decides what it is.

marks.label: T12
marks.text: Goes through [the T12 check](check-a-t12) before it is used.

marks.label: Other
marks.text: Anything else: kept, and used for no figure.

steps.text: Click **Add files**, pick one or more files in the window that opens, and click **Open**. Each file is saved to the property’s folder and listed. Here a made-up loan agreement, added as **Loan agreement**.

marks.label: The file
marks.text: Its name as you saved it; under it, its size, the day it was saved, and how much text the app read from it.

marks.label: Type
marks.text: What the file is. See [Change or remove a file](change-or-remove-a-file).

callouts.text: A file with the same name but different content is kept as a copy (“… (2)”), never replaced. The same file twice says “Already on file”. With **Detect automatically**, a rent roll or an agreement that names another of your properties is filed there instead.
You can also drag files from a folder onto the **Documents** box.

next.text: What happens when the file is a T12.
Change a file’s type, save a copy or remove it.
Every part of the Documents box.

pages.title: Check a T12
pages.description: Look over how a new T12 was read, change what is wrong, and save the reading so its figures are used.
pages.intro: Every new T12 is read twice, by the app’s own reader and by Claude (“the AI” in the app’s words), before anything from it is used. When every check of the reader passes and Claude agrees, it is used at once. Otherwise the review window opens, and you decide.
before: Claude connected, for the second reading: see [Connect Claude](connect-claude). Without it, see [When Claude isn’t connected](check-a-t12#when-claude-isnt-connected).

steps.text: On the property’s page, in **Documents**, leave **Detect automatically** in **What you are adding**, or pick **T12**.
Click **Add files** and pick the T12. Here every check of the reader passes on a made-up T12, but Claude reads two rows differently, so the review window opens.

marks.label: The verdict
marks.text: How many of the reader’s checks fail, and whether Claude agrees.

marks.label: What to look at
marks.text: Every failed check (red) and every row Claude reads differently (amber).

marks.label: Save this reading
marks.text: Saves it; its figures are then used everywhere.

callouts.text: Nothing from the T12 is saved or used until you click **Save this reading**.

sections.title: Look at a row Claude reads differently

steps.text: In **What to look at**, click a row number. The table jumps to that row, lit up. Here Claude puts Utility Reimbursements on the expense side; the reader has it as income.

marks.label: Row 17
marks.text: Jumps to the row.

marks.label: The row
marks.text: Amber: Claude reads it differently.

marks.label: Side
marks.text: Income here; Claude says Expense.

marks.label: AI: …
marks.text: What Claude read.

steps.text: Decide from the file which reading is right. To change the row, pick another value in one of its lists. Here Utility Reimbursements moves to its own underwriting line, Utility Reimbursements (RUBS).

marks.label: Underwriting line
marks.text: Changed by you, so the row is marked “yours”.

marks.label: 1 change of yours · clear my changes
marks.text: How many changes you made; the link undoes them all.

callouts.text: The window works out every check again as soon as you change a row.

steps.text: Type the amount in the row’s **Amount used** box, and click elsewhere. Here it is Claude’s reading of Plumbing Repairs. The box turns green, and the note box red.

marks.label: Amount used
marks.text: Your amount (green).

marks.label: why (needed)
marks.text: Red until you write why.

marks.label: AI: …
marks.text: Claude’s reading of this row: the total, and the month it reads differently.

marks.label: A failed check
marks.text: With your amount, the expenses no longer add up to the total the statement prints.

steps.text: Write why in the note box, and click elsewhere. The note is kept with the reading and in the property’s change history.

callouts.text: An amount that differs from the file can’t be saved without a note. **Save this reading** says which row still needs one.

steps.text: Click **Save this reading**. If a check still fails, the app asks first.

marks.label: Some checks still fail
marks.text: How many checks fail.

marks.label: What is used
marks.text: Which figures are used if you save anyway.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Back to the window, to fix the rows.

marks.label: Save anyway
marks.text: Saves the reading as it is.

steps.text: Click **Save anyway** to use the T12 as it is, or **Cancel** to go back and fix the rows. Once saved, its figures are used everywhere.

callouts.text: Saved with a check still failing, your accounts are used as you set them. If you changed no figure, the statement’s printed totals are used, and Underwriting shows the difference.

steps.text: Click **Keep it waiting** to close the window without saving. The T12 is kept, but nothing from it is used yet. Its row in **Documents** says so.

marks.label: T12: Waiting for your review
marks.text: Saved in the folder, but not used yet.

marks.label: Review
marks.text: Opens the review window again.

marks.label: Type: T12
marks.text: Detected as a T12.

steps.text: To review it from Underwriting instead, pick the property there. The T12 waits above the property’s figures, with **Review**.

marks.label: Property
marks.text: The property.

marks.label: … is waiting for your review
marks.text: The file, why it waits, and that nothing from it is used yet.

marks.label: Review
marks.text: Opens the review window.

steps.text: Click **Review**, look over the rows, and click **Save this reading**. The T12 is used at once: its NOI reaches the property’s page, the Portfolio page, the debt sizing and the refinance.

marks.label: T12: Reviewed by you
marks.text: In use. Other words you may see: “Checked by the reader and the AI” (both agreed), “Read by the reader only (Claude wasn’t connected)”, “Being read by the reader and the AI”.

callouts.text: Data Health lists every T12 still waiting, under “T12s that need your review”. See [Fix what Data Health finds](fix-data-health).

sections.title: If the T12 names no property
sections.text: When you add a T12 on a property’s page and its sheet doesn’t name that property, the app asks which sheet is the property’s T12.

steps.text: Pick the sheet that is the property’s T12, or **None — keep it as a document**.

marks.label: A sheet
marks.text: Use this sheet as the property’s T12.

marks.label: None — keep it as a document
marks.text: Saved as an “Other” document; no figure is taken from it.

marks.label: Save it
marks.text: Saves the file with your answer.

steps.text: Click **Save it**. A sheet you picked then goes through the T12 check, as above.

sections.title: When Claude isn’t connected
sections.text: Without Claude, the T12 can’t be checked against a second reading. The app says so and asks what to do; nothing from the T12 is used yet. The window is pictured in [Documents and the T12 check](ref-documents#when-claude-isnt-connected).

steps.text: Click **Use the reader’s reading** to use the T12 as the app’s reader read it. The button is there only when every check of the reader passes. The T12’s row then says “Read by the reader only (Claude wasn’t connected)”.
Or click **Review it myself** to open the review window, or **Keep it waiting** to decide later.

callouts.text: Once Claude is connected, **Read again** in Underwriting reads the T12 with Claude too, and checks it.

next.text: Underwrite the property from its T12.
Every part of the review window.

pages.title: Change or remove a file
pages.description: Change what a saved file is, save a copy of it on your computer, or remove it from the property.
pages.intro: Every file in a property’s **Documents** has a type, which you can change at any time, and every file can be removed. Removing always asks first.

steps.text: On the property’s page, find the file in **Documents**.
Pick the new type in the list on the file’s row. It is saved at once.

marks.label: T12
marks.text: Read and checked as a T12. (The lit type, Loan agreement, is the one it has now.)

marks.label: Other
marks.text: Kept, used for no figure.

callouts.text: Making a file a T12 sends it through [the T12 check](check-a-t12). Taking the T12 type away from the T12 in use rebuilds the property’s numbers from any other T12 on file.

sections.title: Save a copy on your computer

steps.text: Click **Save copy** on the file’s row, and pick where to save it in the window that opens.
Click **Remove** on the file’s row. The app asks first, and says what goes with the file. Here it is the T12 in use.

marks.label: Remove “…”?
marks.text: The file.

marks.label: What goes with it
marks.text: Deleted from the property’s folder; for the T12 in use, its NOI too.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Keeps the file.

marks.label: Remove
marks.text: Deletes it, and rebuilds the property’s numbers.

steps.text: Click **Remove**. The file is deleted from the property’s folder.

callouts.text: Removing the T12 in use takes its NOI off the Portfolio page, the DSCR and the refinance. The numbers are rebuilt from any other T12 on file; otherwise the property has no NOI yet. The automatic backups keep a copy of every removed file: see [Back up and restore](back-up-and-restore).

next.text: Add another file.
Every part of a file’s row.

pages.title: Split a file that covers several properties
pages.description: Say which part of a workbook or a PDF belongs to which property.
pages.intro: A workbook can hold several properties’ statements, one per sheet or one after another, and one PDF can hold several agreements. Such a file never goes anywhere by itself: you say which part is whose, and each property reads only its own part.

steps.text: On one of the properties’ pages, click **Add files** and pick the file. The app lists its parts, and sets each part whose name matches one of your properties to that property. Here a made-up workbook with three sheets, added on Sample Gardens’ page.

marks.label: This property
marks.text: Part 1 names Sample Gardens: set to it.

marks.label: Another property
marks.text: Part 2 names Sample Oaks: it goes to Sample Oaks’ folder.

marks.label: Not linked
marks.text: Maple Court is no property in the app: not ticked, “Don’t link”.

steps.text: Check each part’s property, and change any that is wrong. Tick a part to link it; a part that is none of your properties stays on **Don’t link**.
To give one part to a second property too, click **+ another property** under it. To make a new property from a part, pick **Add as a new property** in its list.

marks.label: A second property
marks.text: Added by **+ another property**: pick the second property, or leave it empty.

marks.label: ➕ Add as a new property “Maple Court (made-up)”
marks.text: Creates that property and links this part to it.

marks.label: Ticked by itself
marks.text: Picking a property ticks the part.

steps.text: Click **Approve**. Each property gets the file with its own part, and each T12 part goes through [the T12 check](check-a-t12) for its property. The file’s row says which part is this property’s, and the T12 line under it where its part stands in the check. Here part 3 was set back to “Don’t link” first.

marks.label: This property’s part: …
marks.text: Which sheet of the file is Sample Gardens’: only its numbers are read for it.

marks.label: Change
marks.text: Asks the question again, to give another answer.

callouts.text: Two parts given to one property are added together.

sections.title: Answer a file that waits
sections.text: A file saved before anyone said which part is whose (by the assistant, say) waits for an answer: none of its numbers are used for the property until you give one.

steps.text: On the property’s page, find the file’s row in **Documents**: it asks which part is this property’s. Click **Answer**.

marks.label: It has 3 parts — which one is this property’s?
marks.text: Its numbers aren’t used until you say.

marks.label: Answer
marks.text: Opens the question.

steps.text: Tick the property’s part, and pick the property in its list. When no part names the property, nothing is set for you.

marks.label: Which part is Sample Pines (example)’s?
marks.text: Pick it below: nothing is set for you.

marks.label: Property
marks.text: Pick “Sample Pines (example) (this property)” on the right part.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: The file keeps waiting.

marks.label: Approve
marks.text: Links the part; its numbers are used from now on.

steps.text: Click **Approve**. The part’s numbers are used from now on.

callouts.text: Data Health lists every file that waits for an answer. See [Fix what Data Health finds](fix-data-health).

sections.title: Split a PDF by pages
sections.text: One PDF can hold several agreements (split it into parts by pages), or one agreement can cover several properties (give the part to each).

steps.text: On the PDF’s row in **Documents**, click **Pages & properties**. Here a made-up two-page PDF on Sample Gardens’ page.

marks.label: Pages … to …
marks.text: The part’s first and last page.

marks.label: Property
marks.text: The property this part belongs to.

marks.label: + Add a part (pages)
marks.text: Another page range, for another property.

steps.text: For each part, type its first and last page, and pick its property. Click **+ Add a part (pages)** for the next part, or **+ another property** to give the same pages to a second property too.
Click **Approve**. The file is copied to each property named, and each property reads only its own pages.

next.text: What happens to each T12 part.
Every control of the parts and pages windows.

pages.title: Read a scanned PDF
pages.description: Add a PDF whose pages are scans, and see which pages were read by OCR.
pages.intro: A PDF is read page by page. A page that is a picture, such as a scan, is read by OCR: the computer reads the letters in the picture. OCR can make mistakes, so the app always says which pages it read that way.

steps.text: On the property’s page, click **Add files** in **Documents**, and pick the PDF.
Watch the card at the bottom left: it shows each page as it is read. You can keep working meanwhile.

marks.label: The reading card
marks.text: One card per file being read: its name, and the page it is on (“reading scanned page 2 of 2”: “scanned page” means it is read by OCR).

marks.label: Stop
marks.text: Stops after this page.

callouts.text: **Stop** saves nothing: add the file again to go on where it stopped (the pages already read are kept). If the app is closed halfway, it goes on reading at the next start.

steps.text: When the card goes away, find the file in **Documents**. Its row says how it was read, with the pages read by OCR in amber.

marks.label: 2 pages · page 2 read by OCR — may contain errors
marks.text: The pages read by OCR (amber), and any page that couldn’t be read.

marks.label: Pages & properties
marks.text: Split the PDF by pages, or give it to several properties. See [Split a file that covers several properties](split-a-multi-property-file#split-a-pdf-by-pages).

callouts.text: A file with no readable text at all says “no readable text” on its row.

next.text: Split the PDF by pages.
Every part of the Documents box.

pages.title: Read the maturity calendar
pages.description: See every maturity, rate reset and interest-only change coming up, and open a loan from its event.
pages.intro: The Maturity & Reset Calendar lists every balloon, ARM rate reset and interest-only step-up in the book, as a list or month by month. Use it to see what comes due next, and which loans need a decision about their maturity.

steps.text: Click **+** at the end of the tab strip, then **Maturity & Reset Calendar**.

marks.text: Opens the menu of tools that open in a tab.

marks.label: Maturity & Reset Calendar
marks.text: Opens the calendar. If it is already open, it brings its tab forward.

steps.text: The calendar opens in a tab of its own, in the **List** view. It is built from every active loan in the book and redrawn whenever a loan changes.

callouts.text: An archived property, and a removed or paid-off loan, are left out of the calendar.

steps.text: Look at the red **Needs a maturity decision** box at the top. It lists every loan that has matured or whose extension is undecided, with its maturity date and balloon.

marks.label: Needs a maturity decision
marks.text: How many loans wait for a decision.

marks.label: A loan waiting
marks.text: Its status, its maturity date and its balloon. Click the row to open the loan.

steps.text: Once the loan is settled, change its status in the loan’s edit form (**Extended**, **Paid off**…). The loan leaves the box. See [Mark a loan out of date or change its status](set-loan-status).

callouts.text: A loan stays in the box, even after its date has passed, until you change its status. **Matured** is set by hand, or by itself once the maturity date has passed; **Extension undecided** is set by hand.

steps.text: Read the four tiles and the **Maturity wall** under them. The tiles count what falls due in the next 12 months; the wall shows how much debt matures each year.

marks.label: Maturing (next 12 mo)
marks.text: Loans whose maturity falls within the next 12 months.

marks.label: ARM resets (next 12 mo)
marks.text: Loans whose rate, and payment, change within 12 months.

marks.label: IO step-ups (next 12 mo)
marks.text: Loans whose interest-only period ends within 12 months.

marks.label: A red bar
marks.text: Debt maturing this year or next: the closest refinancings.

steps.text: Scroll down to **Upcoming events**: every event in date order, grouped by year. A yellow row is within the next 12 months; a pink row is a loan that needs a maturity decision.

marks.label: Within 12 months
marks.text: A yellow row is less than a year away.

marks.label: Needs a decision
marks.text: A pink row: the loan matured or its extension is undecided.

steps.text: Click **Calendar** in the tool bar. Each year is a box; the first year with events is open, showing its twelve months.

marks.label: Calendar
marks.text: The month-by-month view.

marks.label: A year
marks.text: Click its line to open or close its twelve months.

marks.label: An event
marks.text: Edged in red for a maturity, amber for an ARM reset, green when interest-only ends.

steps.text: Click a year’s line to open or close its months. Several years can be open at once.
Point at an event to read its detail. Click **List** to go back to the list.

sections.title: Open a loan from an event

steps.text: Click any event: a row in the list, a card in a month, or a line in the decision box.
The app goes to **Portfolio**, opens the loan, and lights up the event’s payment in its **Amortization Schedule** for a few seconds.

marks.label: Amortization Schedule
marks.text: The loan’s payment schedule, on the loan’s page under Portfolio.

marks.label: The payment
marks.text: The schedule row of the event’s date, lit up for a few seconds. Here an ARM reset: the first payment at the new rate.

steps.text: Click the **Calendar** tab at the top to go back. It stays open, as you left it.

next.text: Show only some lenders, loans or amounts.
Settle a loan that needs a maturity decision.
Every part of the calendar, named.

pages.title: Narrow the calendar down
pages.description: Show only some lenders, loans or amounts, sort the list, and print what you see.
pages.intro: The tool bar at the top of the calendar narrows it down. The filters work in both views and on the four tiles, and they stay while the tab is open.

steps.text: Click **Lender** in the tool bar. It lists every lender in the book.
Tick one or more lenders. Only their loans are shown, and the button says how many are ticked.

marks.label: Lender (1)
marks.text: One lender is ticked.

marks.label: A tick box
marks.text: On: this lender’s loans are shown.

steps.text: Click **Lender** again to close the list. The tiles, the wall and the list now count only those lenders’ loans.
Click **Loans** in the tool bar.
Type part of a name in **Search loans**. Only the loans that match stay in the list.

marks.label: Search loans
marks.text: Type part of a name.

marks.label: The loans
marks.text: Tick one to show only it; tick several to show them together.

steps.text: Tick the loans to show, then click **Loans** again to close the list.

sections.title: Keep only some amounts and sort them

steps.text: Type the smallest amount in the first **Amount** box. Type 5m for 5 million, or 750k for 750 thousand.
Type the largest amount in the second box, or leave it blank for no limit.
Pick an order in **Sort**: **Date** (grouped by year), **Smallest amount** or **Largest amount**.

marks.label: Amount — min
marks.text: Here 50m: only events of $50,000,000 or more.

marks.label: Sort
marks.text: Here **Largest amount**: the list is largest first, and no longer grouped by year.

marks.label: Counted again
marks.text: The tiles, the wall and the list count only the events that pass.

sections.title: Use a tile as a filter

steps.text: Click a tile, for example **Maturing (next 12 mo)**. The list shows only the loans that tile counts, and a line under the tiles says what is shown.

marks.label: The tile you clicked
marks.text: Outlined while it filters the list.

marks.label: Showing …
marks.text: What the list shows now. Click here to show everything again.

steps.text: Click the tile again, or the line under it, to show everything.

callouts.text: Clicking a tile switches to the **List** view.

steps.text: Click **Clear** to remove every filter: the lenders, the loans, the amounts, the search and the tile you clicked.

marks.label: Clear
marks.text: Removes every filter.

marks.label: Print
marks.text: Prints the calendar as you see it now.

steps.text: Click **Print** to print the calendar, or to save it as a PDF from the print window. The tool bar is left off the paper.

callouts.text: **Clear** doesn’t change the view or the order. Set **Sort** back to **Date** yourself.

next.text: Read the decisions, the tiles, the wall and the events.
Every part of the calendar, named.

pages.title: Fix what Data Health finds
pages.description: Open Data Health and work through what it lists: T12s to review, files to sort out, possible duplicates, maturity decisions and missing data.
pages.intro: Data Health shows on one page what the app knows about every property, and what needs you. Each list shows only when it has something in it, so work down the page from the top until every line is green.

steps.text: Click **+** at the end of the tab strip, then **Data Health**. It reads every property’s files first, which takes a moment with a big book.
Look at the lists at the top. Each is something waiting for you; a list with nothing in it shows a green line, or isn’t shown at all.

marks.label: T12s that need your review
marks.text: T12s waiting for you before they are used.

marks.label: Files with several parts
marks.text: Workbooks waiting for you to say which part is whose.

marks.label: Files without a property
marks.text: Files that no property uses any more.

sections.title: Review a waiting T12
sections.text: A T12 is read twice, by the app’s reader and by the AI, before it is used. When a check fails or the AI reads it differently, it waits here, and nothing from it is used until you decide.

steps.text: Under **T12s that need your review**, click **Review** next to the T12.

marks.label: A T12 waiting
marks.text: The property, the file, and why it waits (here the AI disagrees on 2 points).

marks.label: Review
marks.text: Opens the reading.

steps.text: Read what the window lists under the totals: each failed check, and each point the AI reads differently, with its Excel row. Click a row number to jump to that row.

marks.label: The verdict
marks.text: Whether every check passes, and whether the AI agrees with the reader.

marks.label: What to look at
marks.text: Each failed check and each point read differently.

marks.label: The rows
marks.text: The file’s own rows, what the reader made of each, and the amounts.

steps.text: Change what is wrong in the rows, with a note.
Click **Save this reading**. The T12 is used from now on, and it leaves the list.

callouts.text: Not sure yet? Click **Keep it waiting**: the T12 stays on the list, unused. [Check a T12](check-a-t12) shows this window in full.

sections.title: Say which part of a file is whose
sections.text: A workbook can hold several properties’ statements, one per sheet or one after another. The app never guesses which part is a property’s own: until you answer, the file’s numbers aren’t used for it.

steps.text: Under **Files with several parts waiting for your answer**, click **Answer** next to the file.
Tick the part that belongs to the property, and pick the property in the list under it.

marks.label: The part
marks.text: Ticked: this part is linked.

marks.label: Property
marks.text: The property it belongs to.

marks.label: Approve
marks.text: Links each ticked part to its property.

steps.text: Click **Approve**. The file leaves the list, and its part goes through the T12 check like any new T12. It may then wait under **T12s that need your review**.

callouts.text: A part can go to any property, and several parts to one property (they are added together). If you tick a part without picking its property, **Approve** saves nothing and says which part still needs one. See [Split a file that covers several properties](split-a-multi-property-file).

sections.title: Attach files left without a property
sections.text: Files can be left in a folder that no property uses any more, for example after a rename in an older version.

steps.text: Under **Files without a property**, pick the property they belong to in **attach to**.

marks.label: attach to
marks.text: The property to move the files to.

marks.label: Attach
marks.text: Moves them there, after asking.

steps.text: Click **Attach**, then **Attach** in the question that opens. The files move into that property’s folder.

callouts.text: A file with the same name in that folder is kept as a copy, never replaced.
**Delete** deletes the files instead, after asking. It can’t be undone here; the automatic backups keep a copy.

sections.title: Settle a possible duplicate
sections.text: Two properties may be one building entered twice: the same street address and city, or nearly the same name when one has no address. They are never merged by themselves.

steps.text: Read each pair under **Possible duplicate properties**, and why it is listed.

marks.label: The pair
marks.text: The two property names.

marks.label: Why
marks.text: The same address, or similar names.

marks.label: Not a duplicate
marks.text: Two different buildings: the pair isn’t shown again.

steps.text: If the two are one building, rename one to match the other, so they become one property. See [Rename a property](rename-a-property).
If they are two buildings, click **Not a duplicate**. The pair isn’t shown again, here or in Settings.
Find the loan under **Loans needing a maturity decision**: it has matured, or its extension is undecided.

marks.label: Extension undecided
marks.text: An extension is being discussed and not settled.

marks.label: Matured
marks.text: Past its maturity, not extended or paid off yet.

steps.text: Change the loan’s **Loan Status** in its edit form (**Extended**, **Paid off**…), and save. The loan leaves the list. See [Mark a loan out of date or change its status](set-loan-status).

callouts.text: The Maturity & Reset Calendar shows the same loans on top. See [Read the maturity calendar](read-the-calendar).

sections.title: Fill in what a property is missing

steps.text: Scroll down to **Every property**. Properties missing a T12 or units come first.
Read a row’s **Warnings**: what the app still lacks for that property.

marks.label: no T12
marks.text: No T12 in use yet.

marks.label: units unknown
marks.text: Its number of units isn’t in its profile.

marks.label: Open
marks.text: Opens Underwriting for this property.

steps.text: Click **Open** to go to Underwriting with that property picked, and add its T12 there. See [Upload a T12](upload-a-t12).
Fill in its units in the property’s profile. See [Fill in a property’s profile](fill-in-the-profile).
Click **Recompute all figures** at the top right of the page.
Wait while the button reads “Recomputing…”. The line under it then says when, for how many properties, and “manual”.

callouts.text: Recompute after changing files outside the app, or when the **Computed** column shows an older version of the app.

next.text: Check a T12 row by row.
Split a file that covers several properties.
Every part of Data Health, named.

pages.title: Ask the assistant
pages.description: Open the chat, ask Claude about your loans and properties, and point it at one property.
pages.intro: The assistant is a chat with Claude about your own book. It answers from the same figures the app shows and from the files you give it. It can also search the web for the surroundings, such as a market or the weather in a given month, and names where each web fact came from.
before: Claude connected. See [Connect Claude](connect-claude).

steps.text: Click **Assistant** at the bottom right of the window, on any tab. The chat opens over the app; what you were doing stays as it was underneath.

marks.label: Assistant
marks.text: Opens the chat with Claude.

steps.text: Type your question in the message box at the bottom. Plain words are fine: name a property, a lender or a date.

marks.label: Message
marks.text: Your question.

marks.label: Send
marks.text: Sends it to Claude.

steps.text: Click **Send**, or press Enter. Shift+Enter starts a new line instead.
Read the answer. Your question shows on the right, Claude’s answer on the left.

marks.label: Your message
marks.text: What you asked.

marks.label: Claude’s answer
marks.text: Worked out from the app’s own figures. When something is missing, it says so.

steps.text: Ask a follow-up in the same box. The chat remembers what was said.

callouts.text: In a new chat, click one of the example questions to ask it straight away.

steps.text: Pick the property in the list under the chat. **No property — general chat** is for the whole portfolio.

marks.label: Property
marks.text: The property this chat is about.

marks.label: Its documents
marks.text: How many of the property’s saved files Claude can read.

steps.text: Ask your question. Claude reads that property’s saved files first, and the files you attach are saved to it.

callouts.text: Opening the assistant from a loan’s page picks that loan’s property for a new chat. A chat started on a property is saved with that property.

steps.text: Click **×** at the top right of the chat, or anywhere outside it. The chat stays as it is for next time.

next.text: Have Claude make a change, and approve it.
Reopen an earlier conversation.
Every control in the assistant window.

pages.title: Ask the assistant to do something
pages.description: Have Claude make a change in the app, from your words or from a file, and approve it.
pages.intro: Claude can add properties, fill in details, edit loans, import files, run a refinance and more. Nothing changes until you approve its card. Here it fills in a property’s details from a made-up property summary.
before: Claude connected. See [Connect Claude](connect-claude).

steps.text: Pick the property in the list under the chat.
Click the paperclip (**Attach**) and pick the file. It shows above the message box, with how much was read from it.

marks.label: Attach
marks.text: Opens your computer’s file window. Pick one or more files.

marks.label: Attached
marks.text: The files going with your message. The × on a file removes it.

steps.text: Type what you want done with it, and click **Send**.

callouts.text: Attached files are read on your computer: PDF, Word, Excel, text or pictures. When you send, the file is also saved with the property.

steps.text: Read the card Claude proposes. Each line shows the value now (crossed out), the new value, and where it came from: the file, the page and a quote.

marks.label: Old → new
marks.text: The value now, and the value Claude proposes.

marks.label: Where it came from
marks.text: So you can check it.

marks.label: Tick box
marks.text: Only ticked lines are applied.

marks.label: Approve & apply
marks.text: Makes the change.

steps.text: Untick any line you don’t want.
Click **Approve & apply**. The card shows what was done (✓), and Claude reports back.

marks.label: Done
marks.text: What was applied, and what was left out.

marks.label: Claude’s report
marks.text: Claude is told exactly what happened.

callouts.text: The change is saved in the field’s history as “Assistant, approved by You”. **Cancel** on the card changes nothing, and Claude is told you said no. A card that waits for you is never applied by itself.

next.text: Come back to this conversation later.
Check or change the property’s details yourself.
Every part of the Approve card, named.

pages.title: Use saved chats
pages.description: Reopen an earlier conversation, pin, rename or delete it, and keep a long chat quick.
pages.intro: Every conversation is saved on its own, grouped by property. Reopen one to carry on where you left off, or start a new one; the old one stays in **History**.

steps.text: Click **History** at the top of the assistant.
Find the chat. Type in the search box to look through every saved chat, or look under its property’s name.

marks.label: Search
marks.text: Finds words in every saved chat.

marks.label: Group
marks.text: The property (or Portfolio) the chats below belong to.

marks.label: A chat
marks.text: Its title (your first question), how many messages and when.

steps.text: Click the chat. It opens with its messages and its cards as they ended.

marks.label: An old card
marks.text: What was proposed and what you decided. It can’t be approved again.

steps.text: Type your next message. The conversation carries on from where it ended.

sections.title: Pin, rename or delete a chat

steps.text: In **History**, point at the chat. Its buttons show.

marks.label: Pin, Rename, Delete
marks.text: The star keeps the chat at the top, the pencil gives it your own title, and the bin deletes it (after asking).

steps.text: Click the star (**Pin**), the pencil (**Rename**) or the bin (**Delete**).

sections.title: Compact a long chat
sections.text: A long conversation gets slower. **Compact** keeps the facts and frees up room.

steps.text: Click **Compact** at the top of the assistant.
Claude writes a short brief of the conversation, with every property, figure and decision, and carries on from it.

marks.label: Compact
marks.text: Summarizes the chat so far.

marks.label: The brief
marks.text: What Claude keeps from here on.

callouts.text: The full messages stay in the saved chat.

steps.text: Click **New chat** at the top of the assistant. The current chat is kept in **History**, and nothing in your loans changes.

next.text: Ask about your book.
Every control in the assistant window.

pages.title: Connect Claude
pages.description: Turn on the AI features with your Claude subscription, or with an Anthropic API key.
pages.intro: Claude reads each T12 a second time, writes the stories and What to push, and answers in the assistant. Connect it once on this computer. Your Claude subscription is the recommended way: nothing to install and nothing billed per use. An Anthropic API key is the other way, paid as you go.
before: A Claude Pro or Max subscription, or an Anthropic API key from console.anthropic.com.

steps.text: Click **Settings** at the top right of the window. At the foot of the menu, **Claude connection** says **Connected** or **Not set**.

marks.label: Settings
marks.text: Opens the menu.

marks.label: Claude connection
marks.text: Opens the connection window.

marks.label: Not set
marks.text: Claude isn’t connected yet.

steps.text: Click **Claude connection**. Its window says what is missing.

marks.label: Not connected
marks.text: Amber, with what is missing.

marks.label: Connect with your Claude subscription
marks.text: Click it next.

steps.text: Click **Connect with your Claude subscription**. A small sign-in window opens and takes you to your browser.
Sign in to your Claude subscription in the browser. Close the small window once it says you are signed in.
Back in **Claude connection**, the line at the top turns green: **Connected · signed in to your Claude subscription**.

marks.label: Connected
marks.text: The AI features are on.

marks.label: Sign out
marks.text: Disconnects the subscription on this computer.

callouts.text: The assistant has the same choices under **Connection settings**, and shows them by itself when Claude isn’t connected.

sections.title: Use an API key instead
sections.text: Without a subscription, use a key from console.anthropic.com and pay as you go.

steps.text: In **Claude connection**, click **Advanced — use an Anthropic API key instead**.
Paste your key in **Anthropic API key**. It starts with sk-ant- and is hidden as you type.

marks.label: Anthropic API key
marks.text: Your key, hidden.

marks.label: Save
marks.text: Saves it and switches the app to it.

steps.text: Click **Save**. The key is kept only on this computer, and the top line reads **Connected · using your Anthropic API key**.

marks.label: Connected
marks.text: Through your API key.

marks.label: Clear
marks.text: Removes the key from this computer. The app goes back to your subscription when it is signed in.

callouts.text: A saved key is used for every AI feature, even with a subscription signed in. To go back to the subscription, click **Clear**, or pick **Automatic (recommended)** or **Claude subscription** in the assistant’s **Connection settings**.

next.text: Ask Claude about your book.
Use Claude’s stories and suggestions.
Every control in the connection window.

pages.title: Set the portfolio targets
pages.description: Choose the DSCR, LTV and debt yield the Portfolio page measures every property against.
pages.intro: The Portfolio page holds each property to three targets: a minimum DSCR, a maximum LTV and a minimum debt yield. Its tiles, the Coverage vs targets chart and the coverage table all follow them. Set them to your own standard.

steps.text: Click **Settings** at the top right of the window.
Under **Portfolio targets (Home)**, type a new figure in **Minimum DSCR (target)**, **Maximum LTV (target)** or **Minimum debt yield (target)**.

marks.label: Minimum DSCR
marks.text: 1.25× to start.

marks.label: Maximum LTV
marks.text: 75% to start.

marks.label: Minimum debt yield
marks.text: 8% to start.

steps.text: Click away, or press Tab. The Portfolio page measures every property against the new figure at once, and the targets are kept for next time.

callouts.text: These targets are only for the Portfolio page. The refinance’s “Can you?” limits are fixed, and Underwriting sets its own sizing limits for each property.

next.text: See each property against the targets.
Underwriting’s own limits, property by property.

pages.title: Back up and restore
pages.description: Save everything to one file, and put it back from a file or from an automatic backup.
pages.intro: A backup is one file with everything: every loan, every property’s folder (profile, assumptions, T12s, documents), every chat and your settings. Restore it on this computer or another one. The app also keeps backups by itself, a few seconds after a change and before an Excel import or a restore.

callouts.text: A restore replaces your loans, every property folder and every chat. What you have just before it is saved first, as a **Before a restore** backup, so you can switch back.

steps.text: Click **Data**, under the tabs on the right.

marks.label: Data
marks.text: Opens the menu.

marks.label: Back up to a file…
marks.text: Saves everything to one file.

marks.label: Restore from a file…
marks.text: Puts a backup file back.

steps.text: Click **Back up to a file…**. Your computer’s Save window opens.
Pick a folder and click **Save**. The app says what it backed up.
Click **Data**, then **Restore from a file…**. Your computer’s Open window opens.
Pick the backup file. The app says what is in it and what it will replace.
Click **Restore**. The app reloads with the restored data.
Click **Data**. Under **Recent automatic backups**, each line says why it was taken, when, and what it holds.

marks.label: An automatic backup
marks.text: Why it was taken, when, and what it holds. The newest is first.

marks.label: Open folder
marks.text: The folder that holds them on your computer.

steps.text: Click the backup you want. The app says what it holds and what it will replace.

marks.label: What happens
marks.text: What is replaced, and that your data now is saved first.

marks.label: Restore
marks.text: Restores the backup.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Nothing changes.

steps.text: Click **Restore**. The app reloads with the restored data.

next.text: Move loans in and out of Excel.
Upload a backup file as a shared group’s starting data.
Everything in the Data menu.

pages.title: Move loans in and out of Excel
pages.description: Export your loans to a workbook, or add and update loans from one.
pages.intro: Export puts every active loan in an Excel workbook, one column per loan. Import reads a workbook and adds the new loans and updates the ones you already have. Nothing changes until you have reviewed the import and applied it.

steps.text: Click **Data**, then **Export all loans to Excel…**. A preview shows exactly what the workbook will hold.

marks.label: A loan
marks.text: One column per loan. Untick to leave it out.

marks.label: Select all
marks.text: Ticks or unticks every loan.

marks.label: Export
marks.text: Saves the workbook.

steps.text: Untick any loan you want to leave out.
Click **Export**, then save the .xlsx file in your computer’s Save window.

callouts.text: Removed, paid-off and archived loans aren’t exported. The preview can’t be edited: change a loan in the app.

steps.text: Click **Data**, then **Import loans from Excel…**. A list names the details each loan in your sheet needs.

marks.label: The details
marks.text: What each loan needs.

marks.label: I’ve checked
marks.text: Tick it to turn on Choose file…

marks.label: Choose file…
marks.text: Opens your computer’s Open window.

steps.text: Tick **I’ve checked my sheet includes these details**, then click **Choose file…** and pick the workbook.
Check each row’s status: **new** (it will be added), **update** (it matches a loan you have, and something differs), **unchanged**, or **missing data**. Nothing has changed yet.

marks.label: Counts
marks.text: How many of each, and how many need attention.

marks.label: missing data
marks.text: A required detail the sheet didn’t have.

steps.text: Type the missing detail in each amber cell, or click **✕** at the end of its row to leave that loan out. Here the incomplete made-up loan is removed.

marks.label: Ready
marks.text: 1 new, 1 updated, 1 unchanged: nothing needs attention.
Removes that row from the import.

marks.label: Apply import (2)
marks.text: Imports the new and the updated loans.

steps.text: Click **Apply import**. The app saves an automatic backup, adds the new loans and writes the changes to the updated ones. Unchanged loans stay exactly as they are.

callouts.text: An export from the app always imports. Loans can be in rows or in columns, and small differences in the headers are fine.

steps.text: Click **Data**. The backup taken just before the import is listed in amber as **Before Excel import**.

marks.label: Before Excel import
marks.text: Taken just before the import.

marks.label: After …
marks.text: Taken a few seconds after a change, naming it: here the import.

steps.text: Click **Before Excel import**, then **Restore**. Everything goes back to how it was just before the import.

next.text: Back up everything, and restore it.
Change a loan in the app.
Every control in the export and the import.

pages.title: Update the app
pages.description: Check for a new version, and restart into it.
pages.intro: The chip at the right of the header shows the version you have. Click it to check for a new one: the app downloads it by itself, then asks you to restart.

steps.text: Click the version chip at the right of the header (it shows your version). It reads **Checking for updates…**.

marks.label: Version
marks.text: The version you have. Click it to check.

steps.text: If there is a new version, the chip reads **Update available…**, then **Downloading update…** with how far it is. If you are up to date, the app says so.
When the chip turns green and reads **Update ready — Restart**, click it. The app restarts into the new version.

callouts.text: Updates never touch your loans, files, chats or backups.

next.text: Keep a backup of everything.
The version chip and the header.

pages.title: Sign in or create an account
pages.description: Open your group’s data with your account, ask to join as someone new, or set a new password.
pages.intro: With a shared database, your team works on one copy of the loans, properties and files, and the app opens on its sign-in window. Each person has their own account in their company’s group. The group’s admin approves everyone who asks to join.

steps.text: Type your **Email** and **Password**.

marks.label: Email
marks.text: The email address of your account.

marks.label: Password
marks.text: Your password.

marks.label: Sign in
marks.text: Opens the app on your group’s data.

steps.text: Click **Sign in**. The app opens on your group’s loans, properties and files.

callouts.text: Signed in, but in no group yet? The window lets you ask to join from there. See [In no group yet](ref-shared-database#in-no-group-yet).

sections.title: Set a new password
sections.text: If you forgot your password, the app emails you a code to set a new one.

steps.text: Click **Forgot your password?**.
Type your account’s email and click **Email me a code**. A 6-digit code is sent to that address.

marks.label: Email
marks.text: The email of your account.

marks.label: Email me a code
marks.text: Sends the code.

steps.text: Type the code from the email, then your new password twice (at least 8 characters).

marks.label: The code
marks.text: The 6 digits from the email.

marks.label: New password
marks.text: At least 8 characters.

marks.label: Again
marks.text: The same new password.

steps.text: Click **Set the password and sign in**. The app opens on your group’s data.

sections.title: Create an account
sections.text: For someone new: you ask to join your organization’s group, and its admin approves you.

steps.text: On the sign-in window, click **Create an account**.
Type the first 3 letters of your organization in **Organization**, then click its name in the list.

marks.label: Organization
marks.text: The first 3 letters of its name.

marks.label: Pick yours
marks.text: The groups whose name starts with them. Only these can be joined.

steps.text: Type your **Full name** and **Email**, and a password (at least 8 characters) twice.
Click **Sign up**. Your request goes to the group’s admin, in the app and by email.

marks.label: Waiting for approval
marks.text: Your request is with the admin.

marks.label: What happens next
marks.text: The group, its admin, and what to do once you are approved.

steps.text: When the admin approves you, an email asks you to confirm your address. Confirm it, then sign in.

callouts.text: Until the admin approves you, the sign-in window reminds you of your request, and signing in says the account isn’t ready yet.

next.text: The admin’s first sign-in: bring the starting data.
Save a change for everyone in the group.
Every control on the sign-in window.

pages.title: Start the group (admin)
pages.description: Bring the group’s starting data, the first time its admin signs in.
pages.intro: A new group has no data. Its admin uploads the starting data once: the loans, properties, documents and chats on their own computer, or a backup file. From then on, everyone in the group works on that one copy.
before: The group, made by the maintainer with your email as its admin. See [The maintainer](ref-shared-database#the-maintainer).
Your account: **Create an account**, then the group’s name. As its admin you need no approval, only to confirm your email.

steps.text: Sign in. A banner under the window bar says the group has no data yet.

marks.label: No data yet
marks.text: The group is empty. A member who isn’t the admin is told the admin brings the starting data.

marks.label: Upload this computer’s data
marks.text: Opens the upload.

marks.label: You
marks.text: Who is signed in, and their role. Click it for the menu.

steps.text: Click **Upload this computer’s data** on the banner. The window says what goes up.

marks.label: What goes up
marks.text: How many loans, properties and documents, and how big the files are.

marks.label: From a backup file
marks.text: Upload a backup file instead (**Data** › **Back up to a file…**, from any computer).

marks.label: Why
marks.text: Kept in the change history.

marks.label: Not now
marks.text: Closes; the group stays empty.

marks.label: Upload
marks.text: Sends it, file by file.

steps.text: Check the reason in **Why**, or type your own.
Click **Upload**. The files go up one by one, then the app opens on the group’s data. Everyone in the group sees the same, and changes reach every open app by themselves.

marks.label: Online
marks.text: Green: online, live with the group. Blue: a change of yours isn’t saved yet. Amber: offline.

marks.label: Whole Portfolio
marks.text: The whole group’s portfolio.

marks.label: The group’s loans
marks.text: The same for everyone in the group.

callouts.text: Nothing on this computer changes. If people have asked to join already, their requests open as you sign in: click **Close** to decide later. See [Manage members and codes](manage-members).

next.text: Let people in, and choose what each can do.
Save a change for everyone in the group.

pages.title: Manage members and codes
pages.description: Let people into the group, choose what each one can do, and set your approval and offline codes.
pages.intro: The group’s admin decides who is in the group and what each person can do: **Editor** (can change data) or **View only**. The admin also sets two codes: one to approve a member’s change on the spot, and one to keep working offline.
before: You are the group’s admin.

steps.text: Click your name in the window bar. Its menu has the group’s screens.

marks.label: Your name
marks.text: With your role, and how many people ask to join.

marks.label: Asking to join
marks.text: People who asked to join.

marks.label: Members and codes
marks.text: Who is in the group, and your codes.

steps.text: Click **Asking to join**. Each person shows with their email and when they asked.

marks.label: Who asks
marks.text: Their name, email and when they asked.

marks.label: Turn down
marks.text: They get an email saying so.

marks.label: Approve
marks.text: They join as an editor.

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Decide later: the request waits.

steps.text: Click **Approve**. They get an email to confirm their address, then join as an editor.

marks.label: Approved
marks.text: What happens next for them.

callouts.text: Requests also reach you by email. Deciding in either place decides it.

sections.title: Choose what each person can do

steps.text: In the menu under your name, click **Members and codes**.

marks.label: Can
marks.text: Editor or View only.

marks.label: Remove
marks.text: Takes them out of the group.

marks.label: Not signed in yet
marks.text: Approved, but hasn’t confirmed the email and signed in yet.

steps.text: Under **Can**, pick **Editor** or **View only**. It takes effect in their app at once.
To take someone out of the group, click **Remove** and confirm. Their app says so.
Under **Your codes**, type an **Approval code** and an **Offline code**, at least 6 characters each.

marks.label: Approval code
marks.text: To approve a member’s change on their screen.

marks.label: Offline code
marks.text: To keep changing data with no connection.

marks.label: Save the codes
marks.text: Saves both.

steps.text: Click **Save the codes**. A box left empty keeps that code as it is.

callouts.text: The **approval code** is what you type on a member’s screen to approve, on the spot, a change to something you changed. The **offline code** lets you keep changing data on your own computer when the shared database can’t be reached.

next.text: What a member sees when your approval is needed.
Who changed what, and the daily backups.
Every control on Members and codes.

pages.title: Save a change
pages.description: Save what you changed for everyone in the group, with the reason why.
pages.intro: In the shared database, a change is first only on your computer. You say why, then save it for everyone in the group. The reason is kept in the change history, with your name.

steps.text: Change anything: a loan’s terms, a property’s profile, a document. A bar at the bottom of the window lists what isn’t saved yet.
Type why in the bar. Here, a loan’s lender changed.

marks.label: What changed
marks.text: Point at it for the full list.

marks.label: Why
marks.text: Required. Kept in the change history with your name.

marks.label: Save
marks.text: Saves for everyone in the group.

steps.text: Click **Save**, or press Enter. The change is saved for everyone and reaches every open app by itself.

callouts.text: **Undo** in the bar drops your changes: the data goes back to how it was.

sections.title: When the admin’s approval is needed
sections.text: A member who changes something the admin changed needs the admin’s approval. Here Eddie, an editor, changes the lender the admin just changed.

steps.text: Make your change, type why, and click **Save**. A window says the admin’s approval is needed.

marks.label: The change
marks.text: What, its value now, and your change.

marks.label: Approval code
marks.text: Where the admin types their code.

marks.label: Approve with the code
marks.text: Saves at once with the admin’s code.

marks.label: Send to the admin
marks.text: Sends it to the admin’s app.

marks.label: Undo my change
marks.text: Drops it.

steps.text: If the admin is with you, they type their code in **Approval code** and click **Approve with the code**. The change is saved at once.
If not, click **Send to** and the admin’s name (here **Send to Operator**). It pops up in their app. The current value stays until they approve, and you get a note when they decide.
When a member sends you a change, it pops up in your app: who asked and when, why, and the change.

marks.label: Who and when
marks.text: The member who asked, and when.

marks.label: The change
marks.text: What, its value now, and their change.

marks.label: Turn down
marks.text: Nothing changes.

marks.label: Approve
marks.text: Their change takes effect for everyone.

steps.text: Click **Approve**. Their change takes effect for everyone.
Or click **Turn down**, and add a note for them if you like. Nothing changes.

callouts.text: Click **Close** to decide later. The change waits under **Requests** in the menu under your name.

next.text: Find who changed what, when and why.
Set the approval code.
Every control on the bar and the approvals.

pages.title: See the change history and backups
pages.description: Find who changed what, when and why, and put the group’s data back as it was on a day.
pages.intro: Every change to the group’s data is kept: who made it, when, and why. The admin can also put the whole group’s data back as it was on any of the last 30 days.

steps.text: Click your name in the window bar, then **Change history**. The newest changes come first.
Type a name, a property or a reason in the box. Only the changes with those words stay.

marks.label: Find
marks.text: Here, a property’s name.

marks.label: Who
marks.text: Who made the change, and who approved it.

marks.label: Why
marks.text: The reason typed when it was saved.

steps.text: Click **Older changes** to load the next 200.

sections.title: Put a day back (admin)
sections.text: A backup of the group’s data is taken every day and kept 30 days.

steps.text: In the menu under your name, click **Daily backups**. There is one line for each day.

marks.label: Put this day back
marks.text: For the day on its line.

marks.label: Empty
marks.text: Taken before the group had data: nothing to put back.

steps.text: Click **Put this day back** on the day you want.

marks.label: Why
marks.text: Required. Kept in the change history.

marks.label: Put it back
marks.text: Puts the day back for everyone.

steps.text: Type why and click **Put it back**. The group’s data goes back to how it was that day.

callouts.text: Putting a day back changes the group’s data for everyone in the group. Every change it makes is in the change history, with your reason.

sections.title: Needs Attention
sections.text: Soonest first: balloons due in the next 24 months, interest-only periods ending in the next 12 months, rate resets in the next 12 months and loans flagged out of date; then the Refi cards. A card with a pink outline is three months away or less. Scroll the strip sideways to see every card. See [Check what needs attention](check-what-needs-attention).

views.text: Click one: the loan opens, with its schedule at the month of the event.

marks.label: Needs Attention

marks.text: An adjustable rate resets soon: the new rate and the date.

marks.label: Maturity (red)
marks.text: A loan comes due: the balloon to pay off and the date.

views.title: Further along the strip
views.text: Scroll sideways for the rest of the date cards.

marks.label: IO step-up (orange)
marks.text: An interest-only period ends: the new monthly payment and the date it starts.

views.text: Four figures to read, not buttons. Portfolio DSCR = the total NOI of every property ÷ the total yearly principal-and-interest payments of every loan (during an interest-only period, the full amortizing payment is used). marks.text: How many active loans the page covers.

marks.text: What is owed today on every loan; under it, the number of loans and what they were when first made.

marks.label: Weighted-Avg Rate
marks.text: The average interest rate, weighted by balance; under it, the total monthly debt service (payments plus escrows and fees).

marks.label: Portfolio DSCR
marks.text: Total NOI ÷ total yearly loan payments, against your minimum DSCR target.

marks.label: Portfolio Debt Yield
marks.text: Total NOI ÷ total balance, against your minimum debt-yield target.
