pages.title: A loan’s page
pages.description: Every part of a loan’s page: the bar at the top, the tiles, the rate notice, the NOI box, the Loan Record and the payment schedule.
pages.intro: Open a loan (see [Open a loan](open-a-loan)) and its page shows, from the top: the tiles, the rate notice, the NOI box, the property’s profile, rent roll and documents, the Loan Record and the payment schedule. Each picture names its controls.

views.text: The bar under the tabs is the same for every property. **Edit** and **Remove** there work on the property; the Loan Record has its own for the loan.

marks.label: Whole Portfolio
marks.text: Back to the Portfolio page.

marks.label: Specific Property
marks.text: This view: one property and its loans.

marks.label: Select a property
marks.text: Every property, A to Z. Pick one to open its page. The list marks “senior + mezz”, “in a pooled loan” and “no loan yet”.

marks.label: Add Loan
marks.text: An empty loan form, with this property’s name filled in. See [Add a loan](add-a-loan).

marks.label: Add Property
marks.text: Adds a property by its name. See [Add a property](add-a-property).

marks.label: Edit
marks.text: Opens this property’s profile: its units, manager, NOI override. To change the loan, use **Edit** in the Loan Record.

marks.label: Remove
marks.text: Archives this property with all its loans (it asks first). To remove one loan, use **Remove** in the Loan Record.

marks.label: Refi Calculator
marks.text: Opens the refinance for this property. See [Run a refinance](run-a-refinance).

marks.label: The tiles
marks.text: The loan’s main figures (below).

marks.label: Rate notice
marks.text: How a floating or hybrid rate is set this month (below).

marks.label: NOI box
marks.text: The property’s NOI and coverage (below). Further down: the profile, rent roll, documents, the Loan Record and the schedule.

marks.label: Portfolio tab
marks.text: This tab. Tools like Underwriting open in tabs next to it.
Opens Underwriting, the Calendar or Data Health in a new tab.

marks.label: Data
marks.text: Back up, restore, and Excel export and import.

marks.label: Fetch live rate
marks.text: Gets today’s index values (SOFR, Treasuries, Prime).

marks.label: Settings
marks.text: The app’s size, the portfolio targets, this guide and more.

marks.label: Properties
marks.text: How many properties are in the book.

views.text: Eight figures, worked out for today from the Loan Record; you never type them. Change a term and the tiles follow at once.

marks.label: Total Monthly Debt Service
marks.text: What goes out each month: principal and interest, plus the escrows and fees in the Loan Record.

marks.label: Monthly P&I
marks.text: This month’s principal + interest. Under it: interest-only, the phase of a hybrid, or that it amortizes.

marks.label: Current Balance
marks.text: What is owed today, and how many payments have been made.

marks.label: Original Amount
marks.text: The loan amount on day one, and today’s rate.

marks.label: Amort / Loan Term
marks.text: Amortization years / loan years. “Balloon at mo 120” means the rest is due at month 120.

marks.label: Months to Maturity
marks.text: Months left, and the maturity date.

marks.label: Interest-Only
marks.text: The interest-only months at the start (or “None”), and what follows them.

marks.label: Rate Type
marks.text: Fixed, Floating or Hybrid ARM. A hybrid shows its first rate → its rate after the reset.

sections.title: The rate notice
sections.text: A floating loan or a hybrid ARM has a blue notice under the tiles: how its rate is set this month. The rate is captured automatically; there is nothing to do.

views.title: A floating loan
views.text: It re-prices on the 1st of each month: the index plus the spread, kept between the floor and the cap. Future months use today’s value; the projection holds it flat.

marks.label: How it re-prices
marks.text: When the rate changes and which index it follows.

marks.label: This month’s rate
marks.text: Index + spread = this month’s rate. The floor or cap shows when the loan has one.

marks.label: Captured
marks.text: When this month’s rate was taken.

views.title: A hybrid ARM
views.text: Fixed for its first years, then it floats. The notice says how many fixed months are left, or, once it has reset, that it now floats and how often it resets.

marks.label: Its phase
marks.text: Still fixed (with the months left), or now adjustable.

marks.label: The floating rate
marks.text: What the index + margin is this month.

marks.label: Captured
marks.text: When the index value was taken.

views.text: One NOI for the property, the same one Underwriting and the Portfolio page use. (A refinance uses only the T12 or the underwriting approved from it.) It comes from, in this order: your NOI override in the profile, else the T12, else the property’s operating lines, else an NOI typed on the loan. With none, it says “No NOI yet”.

marks.label: Property NOI
marks.text: The property’s yearly NOI.

marks.label: DSCR (combined)
marks.text: NOI ÷ the yearly debt service of every loan on the property.

marks.label: Debt yield
marks.text: NOI ÷ what is owed today.

marks.label: LTV
marks.text: What is owed ÷ the property’s value (NOI ÷ cap rate).

marks.label: Build operating model
marks.text: Opens this property in Underwriting, where its T12 goes (“Open operating model” once it has one).

marks.label: Where the NOI came from
marks.text: Here an NOI typed on the loan, no T12 yet. With two loans it adds “shared by 2 loans”.

views.text: Every field of the loan in one place. Four parts you type, and one the app works out. A dash means empty.

marks.label: Edit
marks.text: Opens this loan’s form. See [Edit a loan](edit-a-loan).

marks.label: Out of date…
marks.text: Flags the terms as no longer right (“Up to date again” clears it). See [Mark a loan out of date](set-loan-status).

marks.label: Remove
marks.text: Takes this one loan out of every total; it can be restored. See [Remove a loan](remove-a-loan).

marks.label: Loan Identification
marks.text: The property, the lender, the loan number; for a pooled loan, its other properties and releases.

marks.label: Loan Terms
marks.text: Amount, rate, dates, term, amortization, interest-only and the index. The schedule is built from these.

marks.label: Escrows & Reserves
marks.text: The monthly escrows paid with the loan.

marks.label: Additional Fees
marks.text: Servicing, trustee and other monthly fees.

marks.label: Debt Service (computed)
marks.text: Balance today, P&I, total debt service, interest-only left, months to maturity, today’s rate.

marks.label: calc
marks.text: Worked out by the app; it can’t be typed.

views.title: The change history
views.text: A field that was changed has **history (N)** next to its name; **Change history** at the top of the record lists every change to the loan. Here the made-up Juniper Flats loan’s At the Reset was changed.

marks.label: Which field
marks.text: The field and the loan.

marks.label: When
marks.text: The day and time of the change.

marks.label: Old → new
marks.text: What it was and what it became.

marks.label: Who
marks.text: Who made the change.

marks.label: Where from
marks.text: Typed by hand, or where else it came from: the assistant, an Excel import, a refinance…

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Closes the window.

sections.title: The payment schedule
sections.text: At the bottom of the page: every month of the loan, from the first payment to the last. Yellow rows are interest-only, the blue row is today, the green row is the balloon (or the last payment).

marks.label: The loan in one line
marks.text: How many months, when interest starts and ends, and that each month is paid on the 1st of the next.

marks.label: First interest payment
marks.text: Jumps to the first payment and flashes it.

marks.label: First P&I payment
marks.text: Jumps to the first month with principal (after interest-only).

marks.label: Colors
marks.text: What the row colors mean: interest-only, today, balloon / final.

marks.label: Schedule CSV
marks.text: Saves the whole schedule as a file that opens in Excel.
The payment number.

marks.label: Accrual Month / Pays
marks.text: The month interest is counted for, and the day it is paid.

marks.label: Days
marks.text: Days in the month: interest is counted on real days (Actual/360) unless the loan is 30/360.

marks.label: Rate
marks.text: That month’s rate. A small tag says where it came from (fixed, the index on a date).

views.title: Interest-only, then principal
views.text: **First P&I payment** jumps here: the last interest-only month (IO tag), then the first month that pays principal too. The payment goes up and the balance starts to go down.

marks.label: IO
marks.text: An interest-only month: the payment is interest only.

marks.label: First P&I month
marks.text: From here each payment also pays principal.

marks.label: Rate tag
marks.text: Point at it to see where the rate came from.

marks.label: Interest Charged
marks.text: Balance × rate × days ÷ 360.

marks.label: Scheduled Payment
marks.text: What is due that month.

marks.label: Principal Paid
marks.text: Payment − interest: what comes off the balance.

marks.label: Ending Balance
marks.text: What is owed after that month.

views.title: Combined position
views.text: At the top of the Loan Record: each loan, and the stack together.

marks.label: The senior loan
marks.text: Click to open only this loan’s page.

marks.label: The mezz loan
marks.text: Click to open only the mezz.

marks.label: Edit this loan

marks.label: Remove this loan
marks.text: Removes only this loan (it asks first).

marks.label: Combined balance
marks.text: Both balances.

marks.label: Blended rate
marks.text: The rate of the two together, weighted by balance.

marks.label: Combined monthly P&I
marks.text: Both P&I payments.

marks.label: Combined LTV
marks.text: Both balances ÷ the value.

marks.label: DSCR — senior only
marks.text: Coverage of the senior loan alone.

marks.label: DSCR — combined
marks.text: Coverage of both loans.

marks.text: NOI ÷ both balances.

marks.text: Without an NOI the coverage figures stay empty.

sections.title: A pooled loan
sections.text: One loan secured by several properties shows a pool panel in place of the NOI box: one loan, one payment, coverage read on the whole pool. See [Add a loan on several properties](add-a-pooled-loan). The NOIs here are made up.

marks.label: Pooled loan
marks.text: How many properties secure the loan.

marks.label: Current balance
marks.text: What is owed on the one loan.

marks.label: Monthly P&I
marks.text: The one payment.

marks.label: Pool NOI
marks.text: Every property’s NOI added.

marks.label: DSCR (pool)
marks.text: Pool NOI ÷ the loan’s yearly debt service.

marks.label: Debt yield / LTV
marks.text: For the whole pool.

marks.label: This property
marks.text: The property whose page this is.

marks.label: Allocated
marks.text: Each property’s part of the loan: the amount typed, or an even split of what is left.

marks.label: Alloc. balance
marks.text: Its part of what is owed today.

marks.label: Alloc. DSCR
marks.text: Each property’s NOI ÷ its share of the debt service.

marks.label: Release…
marks.text: Takes this property out of the pool (below). If the main property is released, the loan moves to the property with the largest share.

marks.label: Released
marks.text: Each property released so far: when, how much was paid down, and whether the payment was recalculated.

marks.label: Its share
marks.text: Its share of today’s balance, by its allocated amount or by NOI. Lenders often ask 105–125% of it.

marks.label: Release price ($)
marks.text: What is paid down on the loan.

marks.label: Date
marks.text: The day of the paydown.

marks.label: After the paydown
marks.text: Recalculate the payment over the amortization left, or keep the payment (the loan pays down faster).

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Closes it; nothing changes.

marks.label: Release
marks.text: Pays it down and takes the property out of the pool.

views.text: A property in the pool with no loan of its own opens with an “In a pooled loan” tag and the same pool panel.

marks.text: This property secures a pooled loan.

marks.label: Profile

views.text: Four parts, from the loan papers. Required fields have a red *.

marks.label: Add Loan
marks.text: A new loan. Editing a loan says “Edit Loan”.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Closes the form. Nothing is saved.

marks.label: Save Loan
marks.text: Checks the form and saves the loan; its page opens.

marks.label: Property Name
marks.text: Filled in with the property you were on. A new name makes a new property.

marks.label: Loan Identification
marks.text: Who and what (below).

marks.label: Loan Terms
marks.text: The terms from the loan papers (below).

marks.label: Escrows & Reserves

marks.label: Additional Fees

marks.label: Save Loan
marks.text: Try again once it’s fixed.

views.text: Who and what: the property, its address and type, the lender and the loan number.

marks.label: Property Name
marks.text: The property this loan is on. Start typing to pick one you already have.

marks.label: Property Address

marks.label: Property Type
marks.text: Office, Retail, Industrial, Multifamily, Mixed-Use or Other.

marks.label: Lender Name
marks.text: Who lent the money.

marks.label: Its main property

marks.label: How many

marks.label: Tick a property

marks.label: allocated $

marks.label: New — added when you save

marks.label: Has its own loan
marks.text: A property can be in a pool and still have its own loan.

marks.label: Add to this loan

marks.label: Allocated so far
marks.text: The allocated amounts added up, against the loan amount.

sections.title: Loan Terms
sections.text: The terms from the loan papers. The fields change with the **Rate Type**.

views.title: A new fixed loan
views.text: A new fixed loan takes its rate from an index + your spread, and the green line shows the rate it will lock. For a loan that already exists, tick **This is a historical loan** and type its rate instead.

marks.label: Historical loan
marks.text: Tick it for a loan that already exists: you type its real locked rate. Leave it off for a new loan. (Fixed loans only.)

marks.label: Original Loan Amount
marks.text: The amount on day one. Required.

marks.label: Rate Type
marks.text: Fixed, Floating or Hybrid ARM. The fields below change to match.

marks.label: Lien Position
marks.text: Senior, or Mezzanine (paid after the senior).

marks.label: Loan Status
marks.text: Leave blank: it reads Active, or Matured after the maturity date. See [change its status](set-loan-status#change-the-status).

marks.label: Origination Date
marks.text: When the loan closed. Required.

marks.label: First Payment Date
marks.text: The first payment of any kind; an interest-only one counts. Required.

marks.label: Maturity Date
marks.text: From the papers. The schedule is anchored to it.

marks.label: Loan Term (Months)
marks.text: Months until the balloon. Required.

marks.label: Amortization Period
marks.text: Months the payment is worked out over, e.g. 360 for 30 years. Not needed for a loan that is interest-only for its whole term.

marks.label: Day-Count
marks.text: Actual/360 (interest on real days) or 30/360 (the same every month).

marks.label: Amortization Type
marks.text: Level (normal), Fixed Principal, or Fixed P&I (a set payment from the papers).

marks.label: Interest-Only Period
marks.text: Months of interest only at the start. 0 if none.

marks.label: Index
marks.text: The index the rate is built on (SOFR, Prime, a Treasury…).

marks.label: Spread
marks.text: Your margin over the index, in %.

marks.label: Locked rate
marks.text: Index today + spread = the rate this new loan locks.

views.title: A hybrid ARM
views.text: Fixed for its first years, then it floats. With **Fixed P&I** it also asks what the payment does at the reset; see [Set what the payment does at the reset](set-the-reset).

marks.label: Hybrid ARM
marks.text: Fixed first, then it floats.

marks.label: Annual Interest Rate
marks.text: The fixed rate of the first years.

marks.label: Fixed P&I
marks.text: A set monthly payment from the papers.

marks.label: Fixed Amortization Payment
marks.text: That set payment.

marks.label: At the Reset
marks.text: Keep the stated payment, or recalculate it over the remaining amortization.

marks.label: Initial Fixed Period
marks.text: Months at the fixed rate (60 = 5 years).

marks.label: Adjustment Frequency
marks.text: How often the rate resets after that.

marks.label: Index
marks.text: The index the rate follows after the fixed years.

marks.label: Index Value
marks.text: Filled from the live index by itself; type a value only to override it. Offline it says it couldn’t fetch.

marks.label: Spread
marks.text: The margin over the index after the reset.

marks.label: Floor
marks.text: The rate never goes below this.

marks.label: Cap
marks.text: The rate never goes above this.

marks.label: On 1-Month LIBOR Until
marks.text: Only for a loan that started on LIBOR: the last day LIBOR set its rate.

marks.label: Spread Over LIBOR
marks.text: Blank = the same spread as above.

views.text: Monthly amounts paid with the loan. Leave any you don’t have empty. They add to Total Monthly Debt Service.

sections.title: Claude’s stories
sections.text: Under the table. Claude reads the T12 account by account, month by month, with the rent roll, the loan agreement and the property details, and searches the web around the property. It offers stories a lender would accept: only ones that raise the NOI, and only ones it confirmed. Nothing goes in until you open the account and save it. See [Use Claude’s stories and suggestions](use-claudes-stories).

marks.label: Look again
marks.text: Asks Claude again (**Find stories with Claude** the first time). Needs Claude connected.

marks.label: A story
marks.text: One account, one change, its kind and story, and how much it raises the NOI.

marks.label: How Claude got the number
marks.text: From the statement’s own figures.

marks.label: To back it with the lender
marks.text: What you show the lender to prove it.

marks.label: Checked
marks.text: What Claude checked before it suggested this: the T12’s months, the rent roll, the loan agreement, the property details, or a web page with its site and date. A story it couldn’t confirm is never shown.

marks.label: Claude didn’t have
marks.text: Shows only when one of Claude’s four sources is missing: the T12, the rent roll, the loan agreement or the property details (units, address). Claude worked from what it had; add the missing one and click **Look again**.

marks.label: The web
marks.text: How many times Claude searched the web for this, and what it searched.

marks.label: Put it in the draft
marks.text: Opens the account with the story filled in, to check and save.

marks.label: In the pro forma ✓
marks.text: Already in the draft.

views.text: Under Claude’s stories, per property. They don’t change the underwriting by themselves: a line that runs worse than an assumption gets a suggestion in the draft (never one that lowers the NOI), and the reserves per unit are taken off Safe and Aggressive. Each change is kept in the property’s history.

marks.label: Vacancy
marks.text: When the T12 runs above it, the vacancy account gets a suggestion at it; when the T12 already runs below it, a warning. Never applied by itself.

marks.label: Management fee
marks.text: As a % of effective gross income: a suggestion when the T12 runs above it, a warning when it would lower the NOI.

marks.label: Reserves / unit
marks.text: Replacement reserves a year per unit, taken off Safe and Aggressive.

marks.label: Payroll / unit
marks.text: Your payroll benchmark for this property. A payroll line 15% off it is flagged.

marks.label: In-place NOI

marks.label: Underwriting NOI — Safe · Aggressive

views.text: Every property: units, loans, in-place NOI, the approved Safe and Aggressive underwriting NOI (blank until approved), balance, yearly debt service, DSCR, debt yield, LTV and maturity, with a total row.

marks.label: In-place NOI
marks.text: Each property’s NOI.

marks.label: Safe UW NOI

marks.label: Aggressive UW NOI

sections.title: What to push
sections.text: At the bottom of the tab. It runs by itself once the underwriting is approved, and again when you approve again; before that it reads “Approve the underwriting first”. Claude reads the same four sources as for the stories — the T12, the rent roll, the loan agreement and the property details — with the approved underwriting, and searches the web around the property. These pushes are your plan, not the lender’s. See [See what you can still push](use-what-to-push).

marks.label: Re-analyse
marks.text: Asks Claude again.

marks.label: A push
marks.text: What to do, why (from this property’s own figures) and the effort.

marks.label: Its effect, three ways
marks.text: On the in-place T12, on Safe and on Aggressive, each net of what that version already counts. Claude’s estimates: a starting point, not advice.

marks.label: The lever
marks.text: What it pulls: never one a story in the underwriting already pulls.

marks.label: Beside the story
marks.text: The underwriting story it sits next to: a different lever, so both count.

marks.label: Checked
marks.text: What Claude checked before it suggested this push. One it couldn’t confirm is never shown.

marks.label: Claude didn’t have
marks.text: Shows only when one of the four sources is missing: the T12, the rent roll, the loan agreement or the property details. Claude worked from what it had; add the missing one and click **Re-analyse**.

marks.label: The web
marks.text: How many times Claude searched the web for this, and what it searched.

callouts.text: Claude works out who pays the utilities from the T12: a utilities line big enough for the whole property means the owner pays, in the rent, so no billing them back; one only big enough for the common areas means the residents pay their own. There is no push toward 100% occupancy, and next year’s rent growth at the market’s usual rate is measured on top of the underwritten rent.

pages.title: The pro forma window
pages.description: The window that opens over the Underwriting tab: a line’s accounts, every way to change one, the suggestions, and the windows for a new account, the revenue credit and the lender file.
pages.intro: Click a figure in the Underwriting column, or a tool in the underwriting bar, and this window opens over the tab, about 80% of the screen. Nothing in it is saved until you click its save button. Point at a number, on the picture or in the list, to find it.

views.text: Opened by a figure in the **Underwriting** column. On top, the line in the T12, in Safe and in Aggressive. Below, every account of the line — none hidden, a $0 one too — with its 12 months as the statement shows them.

marks.label: The line
marks.text: The whole line in the T12, in Safe and in Aggressive, each per unit.

marks.label: An account
marks.text: Its row in the file, its 12 months, its T12, Safe and Aggressive. Click it to change it.

marks.label: T12
marks.text: The account’s year in the statement.

marks.label: Safe / Aggressive
marks.text: The account in each version; a changed one in bold.

marks.label: A change’s tag
marks.text: Where the change applies and its kind. Hover it to read the story.

marks.label: A $0 account
marks.text: Shown with its twelve zeros: nothing is hidden.

marks.label: The line
marks.text: Each month and each column added up.

marks.label: + Add an account the T12 doesn’t have
marks.text: For money the statement has no account for.
Closes the window.

sections.title: Ways to change an account
sections.text: Click an account and its choices open right under it. Each change has a kind, the versions it applies to and a story. See [Change an account](change-an-account).

views.title: The choices
views.text: Which ways show depends on the account: **% of revenue**, for one, only on an expense or a rent deduction.

marks.label: New amount
marks.text: Type the account’s new yearly figure. Type 0 to take it out: the lender’s file then reads “Took out”.

marks.label: Spread over years
marks.text: A cost paid once every few years counts only its share for one year.

marks.label: Annualize
marks.text: The account becomes its last 3, 6 or 12 months × 12 ÷ the months.

marks.label: % of revenue
marks.text: The account as a % of revenue (expenses and rental deductions).

marks.label: Per unit
marks.text: A dollar figure per apartment a year × the units.

views.title: New amount, kind and story
views.text: Here the snow-removal change, opened again with **Edit**. The preview shows the account’s 12 months before and after, the line and the NOI.

marks.label: Its new amount
marks.text: The yearly figure for this account.

marks.label: Kind
marks.text: Why it changes: non-recurring, spread over years, normalized, operating change, market norm or partnership/back-office (and revenue credit when you annualize income).

marks.label: Apply to
marks.text: Safe, Aggressive or Both.

marks.label: Same story as…
marks.text: The stories already in this underwriting, with their account. Pick one and it fills in.

marks.label: Story
marks.text: The reason the lender reads. Required.

marks.label: Draft it with Claude
marks.text: Claude writes a first draft from the account’s months; you edit it.

marks.label: Before → after
marks.text: The account’s 12 months in the T12 and after the change (each month in proportion).

marks.label: ready to save
marks.text: Or what is still missing.

marks.label: Save
marks.text: **Save the change**, or **Save the edit** for one you opened with Edit. The window stays open on the line.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Closes the choices without saving.

views.title: Spread over years
views.text: For a cost paid once every few years that landed in this T12. Exterior painting cost $14,400 in May and is done every 5 years: the underwriting counts $14,400 ÷ 5 = $2,880 a year. It divides the whole account; for an account that mixes normal monthly costs with one big bill, use **New amount** instead.

marks.label: Paid every … years
marks.text: How often it is paid; it counts one share a year.

marks.label: Kind
marks.text: Set to “Spread over years” by itself.

marks.label: Before → after
marks.text: $14,400 in May becomes $2,880 for the year.

views.title: Annualize
views.text: When an account runs differently in its recent months — a new contract, a rent increase — it becomes its last 3, 6 or 12 months × 12 ÷ the months. Each choice shows what it gives. On a normal 12-month T12 the last 12 months are the T12 itself, so that choice is greyed (“same as the T12”).

marks.label: Last 3 months
marks.text: × 4: here $28,400 a year.

marks.label: Last 12 months
marks.text: Only different from the T12 when the file has more than 12 months, or the T12 rule used the last 3 months × 4.

marks.label: Months used
marks.text: The months it comes from.

marks.label: Kind
marks.text: Operating change for an expense; Revenue credit for an income account.

views.title: % of revenue
views.text: An expense as a % of that version’s effective gross income, or a rent deduction (vacancy, bad debt) as a % of gross potential rent. Because you chose it, it moves when that version’s revenue moves. The management fee never moves by itself.

marks.text: The percentage.

marks.label: It follows revenue
marks.text: Only because you picked % of revenue.

marks.label: The management fee
marks.text: Stays at the T12 unless you change its account.

views.title: Per unit
views.text: A dollar figure per apartment a year, times the units (120 here): for a cost quoted per unit, such as a maintenance role or turnover.

marks.label: $ per unit a year
marks.text: × the property’s units.

marks.label: Aggressive
marks.text: Here only in the Aggressive version.

marks.label: Preview
marks.text: Safe unchanged; Aggressive $300 × 120 = $36,000.

views.title: A suggestion on an account
views.text: When a line runs worse than your assumption, its biggest account gets a suggestion at the assumption, with a ready story, and a **Suggested** chip in its row (**Claude suggests** for one of Claude’s stories). Here the management fee runs 3% of revenue against an assumption of 2.5%. A suggestion only ever raises the NOI, and nothing is applied by itself.

marks.label: Suggested
marks.text: A suggestion waits on this account.

marks.label: The suggestion
marks.text: The change, its kind, the ready story and why.

marks.label: Use this
marks.text: Fills the change and its story in; you can still edit them before you save.

marks.label: Not this one
marks.text: Sets it aside (**Bring it back** undoes it).

views.title: Every suggestion in one list
views.text: Opened by the yellow **suggestions** button in the underwriting bar: every open suggestion, from your assumptions and from Claude.

marks.label: A suggestion
marks.text: Where, what and its story.

marks.label: Open the account
marks.text: Opens the line with the suggestion filled in.

views.text: Opened by **+ Add an account** in the underwriting bar: every line by section — rental income and deductions, other income, expenses — the ones in your T12 first. Pick the line, then name the account and fill it in like any other change. See [Add an account](add-an-account).

marks.label: A line in the underwriting
marks.text: The new account goes under it.

marks.label: A line the T12 doesn’t have
marks.text: Marked “(not in the T12)”: an account here adds the line to the underwriting.

views.text: Opened by **Revenue credit…** in the underwriting bar: every revenue account annualized at once from its last months, for when the property runs better now than the year shows. The table shows each revenue line month by month, the months used highlighted, the T12 and the annualized figure; with a rent roll, today’s occupancy too. A story is required. The management fee doesn’t follow it.

marks.label: Safe / Aggressive (its own)
marks.text: Aggressive can have its own; until then it uses Safe’s.

marks.label: T3 / T6 / T12
marks.text: How many recent months. T12 changes nothing on a normal 12-month file.

marks.label: Months used
marks.text: Which months.

marks.label: Annualized
marks.text: Each line after the credit.

marks.label: Story
marks.text: The reason the lender reads.

marks.label: Save the revenue credit
marks.text: Saves it.

views.text: Opened by **For the lender…** in the underwriting bar: an Excel file with four sheets — **Pro forma** (each line with its change, kind and story, and the reserves), **Changed accounts**, **Reconciliation** and **Monthly** (the months used for the revenue credit marked). See [Approve the underwriting](approve-the-underwriting#give-the-lender-the-file).

marks.label: Safe only
marks.text: One version.

marks.label: Safe and Aggressive
marks.text: Both, side by side.

marks.label: Save the Excel file…
marks.text: Asks where to save “<property> — Pro forma — <date>.xlsx”.

pages.title: The refinance page
pages.description: Every figure and control on a loan’s refinance: today’s loan, coverage, what to push, the verdict, the rate and limits, presets, the proposed loan, the extension and packages.
pages.intro: The refinance opens from a loan’s page with **Refi Calculator** and takes its place. From the top: today’s loan and the kind of deal, coverage and value, what to push, the verdict with the proposed rate and the lender’s limits, then the proposed loan or the extension. The pictures use the app’s sample loans with made-up T12s. Point at a number, on the picture or in the list, to find it.

sections.title: Today’s loan
sections.text: The top of the refinance: the buttons, what you owe today, and the kind of deal.

views.title: The refinance screen
views.text: Everything is worked out live: change a box and the answers update at once. Your choices (the lender’s limits, an appraisal, the kind of deal) are kept with the property for the whole team.

marks.label: Refinance Analysis
marks.text: The loan, and the question: should you refinance?

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Back to the loan’s page. Closing saves nothing and loses nothing.

marks.label: Save as a loan
marks.text: Shown when there is a loan to propose. Saves it as a new loan and marks today’s loan Paid off (refinanced); it asks first. With a pay-down it says the cash you pay in. See [Save the refinance as a loan](save-the-refinance).

marks.label: Refi Calculator (greyed)
marks.text: Greyed while the refinance is open.

marks.label: What kind of deal?
marks.text: A new loan, or an extension with today’s lender.

views.title: Current Loan
views.text: The facts of today’s loan, from its record.

marks.label: Payoff balance
marks.text: What you owe today: what a new loan has to pay off.

marks.label: Current rate
marks.text: Today’s interest rate.

marks.label: Monthly P&I
marks.text: Today’s monthly principal and interest.

marks.label: Remaining
marks.text: Months until today’s loan ends.

marks.label: Matures
marks.text: The date today’s loan is due.

marks.label: Rate reset
marks.text: For a hybrid loan: when the fixed rate ends, what it resets to and the new payment.

views.title: What kind of deal?
views.text: Pick this first: everything below follows it. Each kind keeps its own limits, so switching back and forth loses nothing.

marks.label: New loan
marks.text: The verdict, the limits and the schedule below are a new loan’s, which replaces today’s loan(s).

marks.label: Extend with today’s lender
marks.text: Judge an extension instead: today’s lender keeps the loan on new terms, perhaps after a pay-down. See [The extension](ref-refinance#the-extension).

sections.title: Coverage & value
sections.text: Today’s loan measured on the property’s NOI: the figures a lender looks at first. They are screening estimates; confirm them with the loan documents and a rate sheet.

marks.label: NOI basis
marks.text: Which NOI the refinance is sized on: here In-place T12, from the property’s T12 (made-up). Safe and Aggressive are greyed until the underwriting is approved.

marks.label: Annual NOI
marks.text: The yearly NOI used: from the T12, or the approved underwriting. A typed NOI never sizes a refinance.

marks.label: Cap rate
marks.text: Values the property: value = NOI ÷ cap rate.

marks.label: Est. value
marks.text: The estimated value. An appraisal you type replaces it.

marks.label: LTV today
marks.text: Loan-to-value: what you owe ÷ the value.

marks.label: Debt service today
marks.text: A year of today’s payments.

marks.label: DSCR today
marks.text: Debt coverage: NOI ÷ a year of payments. Lenders usually want 1.25× or more.

marks.label: Interest-only DSCR
marks.text: Coverage on an interest-only payment, which some lenders size on.

marks.label: Debt yield today
marks.text: NOI ÷ what you owe, which insurance companies and CMBS lenders look at.

marks.label: Coverage today
marks.text: Whether today’s coverage clears your DSCR floor.

marks.label: Cap rate
marks.text: Opens a small window to change the cap rate.

marks.label: Credit tier
marks.text: How a lender would grade today’s numbers. Below the floor, the line under it says which test fails; a strong tier takes basis points off the proposed spread.

marks.label: Why it is below the floor
marks.text: Each test that fails against your floor or ceiling: DSCR, LTV, debt yield. Shown only when one fails.

marks.label: Exit cost — penalty type
marks.text: How the early-payoff penalty is worked out. See Exit cost below.

marks.label: Exit cost
marks.text: The early-payoff penalty in dollars today (and as a % of the balance).

marks.label: Capital stack
marks.text: Links a mezzanine or senior loan on the same property. See Capital stack below.

marks.label: How these are worked out
marks.text: The formulas behind the figures above.

views.title: Cap rate
views.text: **Cap rate** changes only the cap rate that values the property. The NOI comes from the T12 or the approved underwriting, picked with the NOI basis; it is never typed here.

marks.label: Refinance — cap rate
marks.text: This window changes the cap rate only.

marks.label: Where the NOI comes from
marks.text: The T12, or the approved underwriting: the NOI basis on the Coverage card.

marks.label: Cap rate (%)
marks.text: Value = NOI ÷ cap rate; it sets the loan-to-value.

marks.label: Continue
marks.text: Saves the cap rate and updates the whole analysis.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Closes without changing anything.

views.title: Exit cost
views.text: Paying today’s loan off early usually costs a penalty. The app estimates it from the type of penalty in the loan; **assumed** means nobody has confirmed the type yet.

marks.label: Penalty type
marks.text: Yield Maintenance (the default), Step-down (a % of the balance that falls each year), Defeasance (a quoted figure), or Open / at par (no penalty). Picking one confirms it and saves it on the loan.

marks.label: Assumed
marks.text: Shown until you pick the type: the estimate uses yield maintenance.

marks.label: Prepay basis
marks.text: How the estimate was worked out; for yield maintenance, today’s Treasury, the months left and the 1% floor.

marks.label: Exit cost
marks.text: The estimated penalty in dollars. Confirm the real figure from the loan documents.

marks.label: As % of balance
marks.text: The same penalty as a share of what you owe.

views.title: Step-down
views.text: A step-down penalty asks for this year’s % of the balance.

marks.label: Step-down
marks.text: Picked here.

marks.label: This year’s step-down
marks.text: This year’s %, for example 3 in year 1 of a 3-2-1 schedule. The exit cost follows.

views.title: Defeasance
views.text: A defeasance takes the figure you were quoted by the lender or the consultant. Until you type one, a yield-maintenance estimate stands in.

marks.label: Defeasance
marks.text: Picked here.

marks.label: Quoted figure
marks.text: The defeasance cost you were quoted, in dollars.

views.title: Capital stack
views.text: When the property also has a mezzanine (or senior) loan, link it here: leverage and coverage are then read on the combined debt.

marks.label: Link a loan
marks.text: The other loan on the same property (None = this loan alone). Agency senior loans don’t allow subordinate debt.

views.title: The NOI basis
views.text: Villages of Whitewater has a made-up T12 and an approved underwriting, so its refinance can be sized on three NOIs. Pick one; everything below follows, and the pick is kept with this refinance for the whole team.

marks.label: In-place T12
marks.text: The NOI as the property runs today, from its T12.

marks.label: Safe underwriting
marks.text: The approved Safe underwriting: the T12 with the changes and stories you approved, after replacement reserves. The starting choice once it is approved.

marks.label: Aggressive underwriting
marks.text: The approved Aggressive version, after reserves.

marks.label: Which months
marks.text: How the T12’s NOI was worked out.

marks.label: What it is sized on
marks.text: Which NOI the analysis uses, and who approved the underwriting and when. Without an approved underwriting, only In-place T12 is offered.

sections.title: What to push
sections.text: Your planning tool, not the lender’s: tick what you would push, pick the amount you need to cover, and see what loan it gets you. The pushes are Claude’s, from **What to push** in Underwriting. See [Plan what to push for a refinance](plan-what-to-push).

views.title: What to push — what it would get you
views.text: Each push has three effects (on the in-place T12, on Safe and on Aggressive), net of what each already counts. Ticking one adds its effect on the NOI basis picked above.

marks.label: What to push — what it would get you
marks.text: Your plan: the coverage, the verdict and the proposed loan follow what you tick.

marks.label: The amount to cover
marks.text: What the loan has to cover, and the NOI that covers it. See the next picture.

marks.label: A push
marks.text: Tick to add it to the NOI used here; untick to take it out.

marks.label: Its effects
marks.text: First what it adds on the basis picked (here Safe), then on each basis: in-place, Safe, Aggressive. The same push is worth less on an underwriting that already counts part of it.

marks.label: Your own lever — name
marks.text: Something you expect to add, for example paid parking.

marks.label: Your own lever — dollars a year
marks.text: What it adds a year. It counts the same on any basis; a negative amount takes NOI away.

marks.label: Add
marks.text: Adds your lever to the list, ticked.

views.title: The amount to cover
views.text: What the new loan has to cover. The line under it says the NOI that covers it at the proposed rate and the lender’s limits, and how far today’s NOI is from it.

marks.label: Today’s payoff
marks.text: What you owe today plus the early-payoff penalty. The starting choice.

marks.label: No penalty — the last 12 months
marks.text: What you will owe 12 months before maturity, when the loan can be paid off without a penalty (today’s payoff if it matures within 12 months).

marks.label: At maturity
marks.text: What you will owe when the loan matures, before its final payment.

marks.label: What it is
marks.text: What the amount picked is made of.

marks.label: The NOI you need
marks.text: The NOI that covers the amount on the basis picked, and how much more that is than today’s.

views.title: Ticked
views.text: A push ticked and a lever of your own added (made-up): the card says what they add to the NOI, and the line under the amount whether that covers it.

marks.label: Added to the NOI
marks.text: What the ticked pushes and your levers add on this basis.

marks.label: Covered — or still missing
marks.text: Whether the NOI now covers the amount, with what is to spare or what is still missing.

marks.label: Ticked push
marks.text: Counted now.

marks.label: Your lever
marks.text: Marked “yours”; tick or untick it like Claude’s.
Removes your lever.

sections.title: The verdict
sections.text: The colored box answers two questions in order: can the property support a loan the size of what you owe, and is it worth doing? The proposed rate and amount, and how the answer is worked out, are inside it.

views.title: Act before … — pay down
views.text: Queens Gate’s rate resets within 12 months and the property can’t support what you owe. The box says so first, with the date, and what it takes: the pay-down to refinance at these limits, or an extension with today’s lender.

marks.label: The answer
marks.text: Act before the reset — pay down $X. The other answers: Refinance, Your decision, Don’t refinance.

marks.label: You owe (payoff)
marks.text: What a new loan has to pay off.

marks.label: Property supports

marks.label: Proposed loan rate

marks.label: Proposed loan amount
marks.text: Starts at what the property supports; type a smaller amount to test it. The line under it shows that loan’s coverage, LTV and debt yield.

marks.label: Can you?
marks.text: Stage one: can the property support a loan the size of what you owe? Here no, and why.

marks.label: How “supports $X” is worked out
marks.text: The NOI, rate, payment and value behind the figure, and the lender’s four limits. See [How much it supports](ref-refinance#how-much-it-supports).

views.title: Refinance
views.text: The Mews at Princeton, with the lender’s spread typed as 0 for the example: the property supports more than you owe, and the lower rate saves more interest than the early-payoff penalty.

marks.text: Both answers are yes.

marks.label: You owe (payoff)

marks.label: Property supports
marks.text: The biggest loan the property supports at the proposed rate and the lender’s limits.

marks.label: Today’s loan rate

marks.text: The property supports at least what you owe.

marks.label: How “supports $X” is worked out
marks.text: The NOI, rate, payment and value behind the figure, and the lender’s four limits. See [How much it supports](ref-refinance#how-much-it-supports).

marks.label: Should you? Your decision
marks.text: The interest saved is less than the penalty, but the cash out is more than 20% of what you owe.

marks.label: Refinance now — with $X cash
marks.text: The cash left after paying off what you owe and the penalty. To take it, click **Save as a loan — Refinance now** at the top.

marks.label: Wait until …
marks.text: Or keep today’s loan until it ends; nothing changes.

marks.label: Your decision.
marks.text: The choice is yours. Lowering the amount so far that the cash no longer covers the penalty is refused with “You can’t do that”.

views.title: Don’t refinance
views.text: The Mint: the property supports less than you owe, and its loan doesn’t end or reset within 12 months, so there is nothing to do yet.

marks.label: Don’t refinance
marks.text: The answer.

marks.label: You owe (payoff)
marks.text: What a new loan has to pay off.

marks.label: Property supports
marks.text: The biggest loan the property supports at the proposed rate and the lender’s limits.

marks.label: Today’s loan rate
marks.text: The rate today’s loan charges now.

marks.label: Proposed loan rate
marks.text: The new loan’s rate, from the rate boxes below.

marks.label: Proposed rate
marks.text: The new loan’s rate type, index and spread. See [Rate & amount](ref-refinance#rate-amount).

marks.label: Proposed loan amount
marks.text: Type a smaller amount to test it. The line under it shows that loan’s coverage, LTV and debt yield.

marks.label: Can you? No
marks.text: What caps it, and what would change it: NOI rising, the rate falling, or a pay-down.

marks.label: How “supports $X” is worked out
marks.text: The NOI, rate, payment and value behind the figure, and the lender’s four limits. See [How much it supports](ref-refinance#how-much-it-supports).

marks.label: Bottom line
marks.text: Don’t refinance: the property can’t support a loan the size of the payoff yet.

views.title: No T12 yet
views.text: Avalon Norwalk has no T12. A refinance is sized on the T12 and the underwriting made from it, never on a typed NOI, so nothing is sized.

marks.label: No T12 yet
marks.text: This property has no T12 uploaded.

marks.label: Why nothing is sized
marks.text: A refinance is sized on the T12 and the underwriting made from it.

marks.label: Upload its T12 in Underwriting
marks.text: Closes the refinance and opens Underwriting on this property, ready for its T12.

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Back to the loan’s page.

sections.title: Rate & amount
sections.text: Inside the verdict box: the new loan’s rate type, index and spread, and its amount. It starts from today’s loan’s type and a usual spread; type your lender’s quote and everything above and below updates at once.

views.title: Hybrid
views.text: A fixed period, then adjustable.

marks.label: Fixed
marks.text: One rate for the whole term: a Treasury matched to the term + the lender’s spread.

marks.label: Floating
marks.text: An index (SOFR, Prime …) + a margin, changing as the index moves.

marks.label: Hybrid
marks.text: Fixed for the first years, then adjustable.

marks.label: Index (fixed period)
marks.text: The Treasury the fixed period is priced on. The list holds every rate the app has; **Fetch live rate** at the top refreshes them.

marks.label: Spread (bps)
marks.text: The lender’s quote in basis points (100 bps = 1%).

marks.label: Index (adjustable)
marks.text: What the rate follows after the fixed period.

marks.label: Margin (bps)
marks.text: The lender’s margin over that index.

marks.label: Proposed loan amount
marks.text: Up to what the property supports; lowering it shows the cash you’d pay in.

marks.label: Rate (fixed period)
marks.text: The index today + the spread. “Built-in rate — fetch to update” means the index is the app’s own figure until you click **Fetch live rate**. The yellow “starting spread” tag says where the starting spread came from (your recent loans of this kind); it goes once you type the lender’s quote.

marks.label: Monthly payment (fixed period)
marks.text: The payment in the fixed years. The verdict and the limits use this rate.

marks.label: Monthly payment (after)
marks.text: The payment after the fixed period if the index stays where it is today, for information only.

marks.label: At this amount
marks.text: The proposed loan’s coverage, interest-only coverage, LTV and debt yield at the amount typed.

views.title: Floating
views.text: Pick the index and type the lender’s margin. The rate is today’s index + the margin.

marks.label: Floating
marks.text: Picked.

marks.label: Index
marks.text: SOFR (overnight or 30-day average), Prime, or a Treasury: every rate the app has.

marks.label: Spread (bps)
marks.text: The lender’s margin over the index, in basis points.

marks.label: Rate floor (%)
marks.text: The lowest the rate can go, whatever the index does. Empty = no floor.

marks.label: Rate cap (%)
marks.text: The highest the rate can go. Empty = no cap.

marks.label: Cap cost (bps/yr)
marks.text: The yearly cost of an interest-rate cap, which floating lenders often require. It starts at 0 until you buy one.

marks.label: Rate
marks.text: Today’s index (and the day it was set) + the spread.

marks.label: Proposed loan amount
marks.text: The new loan’s amount. Switching the rate type works out what the property supports again.

views.title: Fixed
views.text: The Treasury that matches the term, plus the lender’s spread.

marks.label: Fixed
marks.text: Picked.

marks.label: Index
marks.text: The Treasury matched to the loan’s term. Change it if the lender prices on another.

marks.label: Spread (bps)
marks.text: The lender’s spread.

marks.label: Rate
marks.text: The Treasury today + the spread: one rate for the whole term.

marks.label: Proposed loan amount
marks.text: The new loan’s amount.

marks.label: At this amount
marks.text: That loan’s coverage, LTV and debt yield.

sections.title: How much it supports
sections.text: How “supports $X” is worked out, under **Can you?**: the NOI, the rate, the payment and the value, and the four limits a lender sizes a loan on. Each limit allows a loan; the smallest of the ones your lender uses is what the property supports. Your figures are kept with this refinance for the whole team.

marks.label: NOI
marks.text: The NOI used, and where it comes from.

marks.label: Rate
marks.text: The proposed loan’s rate (index + spread).

marks.label: Payment
marks.text: How the payment is figured: amortizing, interest-only months.

marks.label: Amortization and interest-only
marks.text: The new loan’s own: type them here. A new loan starts with no interest-only; today’s loan’s is never copied.

marks.label: Value
marks.text: NOI ÷ cap rate, or the appraisal once you type one. The loan-to-value limit works on this.

marks.label: Appraised value
marks.text: Type an appraisal to use it instead of NOI ÷ cap rate.

marks.label: Dated
marks.text: The appraisal’s date, kept with it.

marks.label: Note
marks.text: Who appraised it, or any note.

marks.label: Lender preset
marks.text: A lender’s saved limits. See [Lender presets](ref-refinance#lender-presets).

marks.label: Lender uses
marks.text: Tick the limits this lender uses; an unticked one is greyed and doesn’t count.

marks.label: Lender limit
marks.text: The limit’s name, how its loan is worked out, and (grey) that loan’s coverage, LTV and debt yield.

marks.label: Debt coverage, amortizing
marks.text: NOI ÷ (this × the loan constant). Lenders often ask 1.20–1.35×.

marks.label: Debt coverage, interest-only
marks.text: Leave blank (not used) unless the lender sizes on the interest-only payment.

marks.label: Loan-to-value
marks.text: The most it lends, as a % of the value.

marks.label: Debt yield
marks.text: The least NOI ÷ loan it accepts.

marks.label: Loan it allows
marks.text: The biggest loan each limit allows on its own.

marks.label: Binds
marks.text: The limit that sets the amount: the smallest one used.

marks.label: The smallest
marks.text: The smallest loan of the limits used: what the property supports.

marks.label: Headroom
marks.text: How much room is left before the next limit would bind instead.

marks.label: Change history
marks.text: Every change to this refinance’s limits, appraisal and deal: when, who, old → new.

views.title: An appraisal and the lender’s own limits
views.text: Typed: an appraised value (a made-up $65,000,000), and Debt yield unticked because this lender doesn’t use it. The loan-to-value now works on the appraisal, and the unticked line is greyed.

marks.label: Value
marks.text: Now the appraisal, with its note.

marks.label: Use NOI ÷ cap rate instead
marks.text: Drops the appraisal and goes back to NOI ÷ cap rate.

marks.label: Appraised value
marks.text: Clear the box to go back to NOI ÷ cap rate.

marks.label: Note
marks.text: Here “Example appraiser (made-up)”.

marks.label: Loan-to-value
marks.text: 75% of the appraisal.

marks.label: Not used by this lender
marks.text: Greyed; it no longer counts. Tick it to use it again. At least one limit must stay ticked.

marks.label: The smallest of the limits this lender uses
marks.text: Only the ticked limits count.

marks.label: Back to the start
marks.text: Puts the limits back to 1.25× / 75% / 7%, all used. Shown once you have changed them.

marks.label: Change history
marks.text: Lists the changes just made.

views.title: Change history
views.text: Every change to this refinance (limits, appraisal, kind of deal, extension terms) with who made it and when.

marks.label: Refinance — change history
marks.text: This refinance’s own list.

marks.label: A change
marks.text: When, what (for example Refinance · appraised value), old → new, who, and where it came from.
Closes the list.

sections.title: Lender presets
sections.text: A list of lenders’ limits kept for the whole group, so you pick a lender instead of typing its numbers. The list starts empty; next to **Lender preset**, the admin sees **Add a preset**, later **Manage presets**. Only the group’s admin edits the list (anyone else gets “Only the group’s admin changes the lender presets”); anyone can pick a preset. See [Use a lender preset](use-a-lender-preset).

views.title: The presets window
views.text: Each preset is one lender. Nothing is saved until **Save the list**.

marks.label: Name
marks.text: The lender, for example Fannie Mae. A preset without a name is dropped when you save.

marks.label: DSCR
marks.text: Its debt coverage on the amortizing payment.

marks.label: IO
marks.text: Its coverage on an interest-only payment (blank if it doesn’t use one).

marks.label: LTV
marks.text: Its most loan-to-value, in %.

marks.label: DY
marks.text: Its least debt yield, in %.

marks.label: Remove
marks.text: Takes this preset off the list.

marks.label: Uses
marks.text: The limits this lender uses.

marks.label: Interest-only sizing
marks.text: Tick if it sizes a loan that is interest-only for its whole term on the interest-only payment.

marks.label: Rate types
marks.text: The rate types it lends at; an unticked one is greyed in the refinance.

marks.label: Longest amortization
marks.text: In years.

marks.label: Penalty on an extension
marks.text: What this lender usually asks when it extends a loan: the full penalty, on the pay-down only, a part (% or $), or none.

marks.label: Part (%)
marks.text: For a part (%): the share of the full penalty (here 50%). A part ($) asks for a dollar amount instead.

marks.label: Notes
marks.text: Anything else worth remembering about this lender.

marks.label: Source
marks.text: Where the numbers came from, and when.

marks.label: Add a preset
marks.text: Adds another lender.

marks.label: Save the list
marks.text: Saves the list for the whole group and closes the window.

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Closes without saving; the changes are dropped.

views.title: A preset picked
views.text: Picked for this refinance: the limits fill in from the preset, the table names it, and a rate type the lender doesn’t allow is greyed in the rate boxes (clicking it says why).

marks.label: Lender preset
marks.text: Pick a lender, or “None — type the limits”.

marks.label: Its name
marks.text: The preset in use; “(changed here)” once you change a limit by hand.

marks.label: Manage presets
marks.text: Edit the group’s list (admin only).

marks.label: What it allows
marks.text: The rate types this lender lends at, and its longest amortization.

marks.label: The limits
marks.text: Filled from the preset (here 1.30× / 70% / 8%). Type over one and its name says “changed here”.

marks.label: What the property supports
marks.text: Worked out again on the preset’s limits.

sections.title: The proposed loan
sections.text: Shown when the answer is **Refinance**, **Your decision** or a pay-down: the new loan’s terms and its payment schedule. It matches today’s term and amortization, with no interest-only unless you type it, priced at today’s rate; every box is editable and the verdict updates as you type. **Save as a loan** at the top saves it; see [Save the refinance as a loan](save-the-refinance).

marks.label: Loan amount
marks.text: Set in the verdict box above.

marks.label: Term (yrs)
marks.text: Years until the new loan is due.

marks.label: Amortization (yrs)
marks.text: Years the payment is figured over.

marks.label: Interest-only (mo)
marks.text: Months of interest-only payments first.

marks.label: Closing (% of loan)
marks.text: Closing costs, as a % of the loan.

marks.label: New monthly payment
marks.text: The first payment, and how it compares with today’s.

marks.label: vs your current
marks.text: Today’s monthly payment, and how much the new one saves (or costs) each month.

marks.label: Escrows & reserves
marks.text: Click to open: tax and insurance escrows, replacement and TI/LC reserves, ground lease, other escrows.

marks.label: Additional fees
marks.text: Click to open: servicing, trustee and other fees.

marks.label: Amortization schedule
marks.text: Every payment of the new loan: rate, interest, payment, principal and balance; interest-only months are marked IO. Scroll inside the box for the rest.

views.title: Escrows, reserves and fees
views.text: Opened: the monthly escrows, reserves and fees that come with the new loan’s payment. Every box here is added to the monthly payment.

marks.label: Tax escrow
marks.text: Monthly real-estate-tax escrow, in dollars a month.

marks.label: Insurance escrow
marks.text: Monthly insurance escrow.

marks.label: Replacement reserve
marks.text: Monthly replacement reserve.

marks.label: TI/LC reserve
marks.text: Tenant improvements and leasing commissions (commercial).

marks.label: Ground lease
marks.text: A ground-lease payment, if any.

marks.label: Servicing fee
marks.text: The servicer’s monthly fee.

marks.label: Other escrow 1
marks.text: Any other monthly escrow.

marks.label: Other escrow 2
marks.text: A second one.

marks.label: Trustee fee
marks.text: The trustee’s monthly fee.

marks.label: Other fee 1
marks.text: Any other monthly fee.

marks.label: Other fee 2
marks.text: A second one.

sections.title: The extension
sections.text: With **Extend with today’s lender** picked, everything below judges the extension instead of a new loan: its own verdict, rate, limits, terms and schedule. Saving it, and undoing it, are shown in [Extend with today’s lender](extend-with-your-lender).

marks.label: Extend with today’s lender
marks.text: Picked.

marks.label: Save the extension
marks.text: Shown when the answer is to extend. Saves the extension on today’s loan, with the pay-down it needs; it asks first.

views.title: The extension’s verdict
views.text: The same rule as a new loan, applied to the extension: the pay-down it needs to fit today’s lender’s limits, and whether it is worth doing.

marks.label: The answer
marks.text: Extend — pay down $X, or Not yet, or Don’t extend now.

marks.label: You’ll owe on …
marks.text: What you will owe on the day today’s terms end.

marks.label: Today’s lender allows
marks.text: The biggest loan today’s lender’s limits allow at the extension’s rate.

marks.label: Today’s loan rate
marks.text: With the reset ahead.

marks.label: Extension rate
marks.text: The index + today’s lender’s spread.

marks.label: Index
marks.text: What the extension’s rate floats on: every rate the app has.

marks.label: Spread (bps)
marks.text: Today’s lender’s quote over the index.

marks.label: Can you?
marks.text: Yes, with or without a pay-down.

marks.label: The pay-down
marks.text: What you will owe less what the lender’s limits allow, and which limit sets it.

marks.label: Today’s lender’s limits
marks.text: The limits table for the extension, kept apart from a new loan’s. See the next picture.

marks.label: Should you?
marks.text: Yes when today’s loan ends or resets within 12 months; Not yet when nothing ends or resets within 12 months; otherwise yes only when the lower rate saves more than the penalty.

marks.label: Bottom line
marks.text: What to do, with the cash it takes: pay-down + penalty + fee.

views.title: Today’s lender’s limits
views.text: Today’s lender’s own limits for the extension (here 1.11× amortizing and 1.35× interest-only, made-up), kept with the property apart from a new loan’s.

marks.label: Amortizing coverage
marks.text: Today’s lender’s DSCR.

marks.label: Interest-only coverage
marks.text: Its coverage on the interest-only payment.

marks.label: Loan-to-value
marks.text: Today’s lender’s most loan-to-value, here on the appraisal.

marks.label: Debt yield
marks.text: Its least debt yield.

marks.label: Lender uses
marks.text: Untick a limit today’s lender doesn’t use.

marks.label: Lender preset
marks.text: Today’s lender’s preset, if the group has one. It also fills in the penalty that lender usually asks. **Manage presets** edits the list (admin only).

marks.label: Appraised value
marks.text: Shared with the new loan’s: one appraisal for the property (here a made-up $65,000,000).

marks.label: What today’s lender allows
marks.text: The smallest of the limits it uses; the binding one is marked BINDS.

marks.label: Interest-only hint
marks.text: The extension is interest-only for its whole term: untick the amortizing line if the lender sizes on the interest-only payment.

marks.label: Back to the new loan’s limits
marks.text: Drops today’s lender’s own limits and uses the new loan’s again.

marks.label: Change history
marks.text: Every change to the refinance, these limits included.

views.title: The extension’s terms
views.text: When today’s terms end, how long the new terms run, interest-only, the amortization after it, the lender’s penalty and the fee, and what it all adds up to.

marks.label: Today’s terms end on
marks.text: Starts at the payment before the rate resets (or the maturity).

marks.label: Months on the new terms
marks.text: How long the extension runs.

marks.label: Interest-only
marks.text: The whole term, the first N months, or none.

marks.label: Amortization
marks.text: Months the payment is figured over after interest-only.

marks.label: Early-payoff penalty
marks.text: What this lender asks: the full penalty, on the pay-down only, a part, or none. Until you pick, it assumes on the pay-down.

marks.label: Extension fee in
marks.text: % of the extended amount, or dollars.

marks.label: Extension fee
marks.text: The fee.

marks.label: Pay-down needed
marks.text: What you pay down so the loan fits the lender’s limits.

marks.label: Extended amount
marks.text: What you owe after the pay-down.

marks.label: At this amount
marks.text: The extended loan’s coverage, interest-only coverage, LTV and debt yield.

marks.label: Penalty
marks.text: In dollars, how it was worked out, and the full penalty today.

marks.label: Assumed
marks.text: Until you pick what this lender asks, the penalty is assumed to be on the pay-down only. Confirm it with the lender.

marks.label: Extension fee
marks.text: The fee in dollars.

marks.label: Cash needed
marks.text: Pay-down + penalty + fee.

marks.label: First payment
marks.text: The date and amount of the first payment on the new terms.

marks.label: New maturity
marks.text: When the extended loan is due.

marks.label: Earlier than today’s
marks.text: A warning: these terms would end before today’s loan does. Type more months if that isn’t what you mean.

views.title: Penalty: a part of it
views.text: **A part (%)** asks what share of the full penalty the lender wants. **The first N months** of interest-only asks how many months.

marks.label: Part of the full penalty (%)
marks.text: Here 40% of today’s full penalty.

marks.label: Interest-only months
marks.text: How many months are interest-only (shown when you pick The first N months).

marks.label: Penalty
marks.text: Now 40% of the full penalty, no longer assumed.

marks.label: Cash needed
marks.text: Follows at once.

views.title: Penalty and fee in dollars
views.text: **A part ($)** asks for the penalty the lender quotes, in dollars; the fee can be in dollars too. Here a made-up $100,000 penalty and a $25,000 fee.

marks.label: A part — a dollar amount
marks.text: The other choices: the full penalty, on the pay-down only, a part (%), none.

marks.label: Penalty the lender asks ($)
marks.text: The lender’s figure.

marks.label: Extension fee in dollars
marks.text: Or % of the extended amount.

marks.label: Fee
marks.text: Counted in the cash needed.

views.title: The payment schedule with the extension
views.text: From today to the new maturity: the pay-down on the date today’s terms end, where the extension starts, and its months shaded.

marks.label: From today to …
marks.text: The whole schedule with the extension in place.

marks.label: Paid down
marks.text: The pay-down, as a principal payment.

marks.label: Extension starts
marks.text: The first payment on the new terms.

marks.label: Extension months
marks.text: Shaded: the new rate and terms.

views.title: Not yet
views.text: The Mews at Princeton: today’s lender’s limits cover what you’ll owe, but nothing ends or resets within 12 months, so the answer is Not yet and there is no **Save the extension**. When a lower rate doesn’t pay for the penalty, the answer is Don’t extend now.

marks.label: Not yet
marks.text: Today’s terms end more than 12 months from now.

marks.label: Can you? Yes
marks.text: Today’s lender’s limits allow more than you’ll owe: no pay-down needed.

marks.label: Should you? Not yet

sections.title: Several loans together
sections.text: A property’s senior and mezzanine loans refinance as one package; **Create a portfolio…** puts several properties under one new loan. Or each loan is extended with its own lender (**Extend with today’s lenders**). See [Refinance several loans together](refinance-together).

views.title: Senior + mezz: the whole property
views.text: The property’s combined entry under **Specific Property** (its name followed by **senior + mezz**), then **Refi Calculator**: one new loan pays off both. Here Avalon White Plains, with a made-up T12.

marks.label: The loans
marks.text: Every loan on the property, refinanced together (they depend on one another).

marks.label: Payoff balance
marks.text: Each loan at its own balance, added up.

marks.label: Monthly payments
marks.text: Today’s payments on all of them.

marks.label: Current rate
marks.text: The loans’ rate together, weighted by what is owed on each.

marks.label: Remaining
marks.text: Months until the first of them ends.

marks.label: Matures
marks.text: When the first of them is due.

views.title: Extend with today’s lenders: the verdict
views.text: **Extend with today’s lenders** on a package: every loan with its own lender, each sized on what secures it. Here K2 Sweetwater (a made-up T12).

marks.label: The answer
marks.text: Extend all of them, some of them now, Not yet, or Don’t extend now — with the pay-down in all.

marks.label: Loan
marks.text: Each loan, senior first, with its lender.

marks.label: Today’s terms end

marks.label: You’ll owe

marks.label: Pay-down
marks.text: What the loan must pay down to fit.

marks.label: Rate
marks.text: Today’s rate → the extension’s rate.

marks.text: Extend (with a pay-down), Not yet, Don’t extend now, or Extended once saved.

marks.label: In all
marks.text: What the loans to extend now owe, allow and pay down together.

marks.label: Bottom line
marks.text: The loans to extend, the pay-downs and the cash needed (pay-downs + penalties + fees).

views.title: Extend with today’s lenders: the limits
views.text: One table for the package: today’s lenders’ limits apply to each loan.

marks.label: Lender preset
marks.text: Fills in a lender’s usual limits.

marks.label: Lenders use
marks.text: Untick a limit the lenders don’t use.

marks.label: A limit
marks.text: Type the lenders’ own figure.

marks.label: Change history
marks.text: Every change to the package’s refinance.

views.title: Extend with today’s lenders: one loan’s card
views.text: Each loan has its own card: its lender’s quote, what it is sized on, and its terms. Here the mezzanine.

marks.label: The loan
marks.text: Its name, its lender and its verdict. Click to fold it.

marks.label: Its lender’s spread
marks.text: Each lender quotes its own rate.

views.title: Create a portfolio…
views.text: On the Portfolio tab, above the Coverage table. Tick every property the one new loan will secure. Nothing changes until you save the new loan on the next screen.

marks.label: Find a property
marks.text: Type to narrow the list.

marks.label: Tick a property
marks.text: Each property the new loan will secure.
