pages.title: Documents and the T12 check
pages.description: Every part of a property’s Documents box, the T12 review window, and the windows that ask which part of a file is whose.
pages.intro: The pictures use made-up properties and made-up files. Point at a number, on the picture or in the list, to find it.

sections.title: The Documents box
sections.text: On every property’s page, with or without a loan: the files saved in the property’s folder.

marks.label: Documents
marks.text: The files saved in this property’s folder.

marks.label: Saved for …
marks.text: Which property. The assistant reads these when you talk about it.

marks.label: What you are adding
marks.text: The type of the next files you add (next picture).

marks.label: Add files
marks.text: Opens your computer’s file window: pick one or more files and click Open. Dropping files on this box does the same.

marks.label: Nothing yet
marks.text: Shown until the first file is added.

views.title: What you are adding
views.text: The same types are in the list on each file’s row, where you can change them later.

marks.label: Detect automatically
marks.text: The app reads the file and decides: a T12, a rent roll, an agreement… A rent roll or an agreement that names another property is filed there instead.

marks.label: Loan agreement
marks.text: The loan agreement. It is read when you ask to fill in the loan from it, and it is one of Claude’s sources for its stories and What to push.

marks.label: T12
marks.text: The operating statement. It goes through the T12 check before it is used.

marks.label: Rent roll
marks.text: The rent roll: units, occupancy and rents.

marks.label: Unit Statistics
marks.text: A unit statistics report.

marks.label: Other
marks.text: Anything else: kept, and used for no figure.

views.title: A file in the list
views.text: Each file is a row: its name, size and the day it was saved, how it was read, its type, and two buttons.

marks.label: The file
marks.text: Its name as you saved it. Under it: its size and the day it was saved, or “no readable text” when the app can’t read any.

marks.label: How it was read
marks.text: How much text was read from it; for a PDF, its pages and which were read by OCR.

marks.label: Type
marks.text: What the file is. Change it here at any time.

marks.label: Save copy
marks.text: Saves a copy wherever you choose on your computer.

marks.label: Remove
marks.text: Deletes it from the property’s folder; it asks first.

marks.label: Folder
marks.text: Opens the documents folder on your computer.

sections.title: The T12 review window
sections.text: Opens when a new T12 fails a check of the app’s reader, or Claude reads it differently. Nothing from the T12 is used until you save. A T12’s row in **Documents** says where it stands: “Being read by the reader and the AI”, “Waiting for your review” (with **Review**), “Checked by the reader and the AI”, “Reviewed by you”, or “Read by the reader only (Claude wasn’t connected)”. For the steps, see [Check a T12](check-a-t12).

marks.label: The file and sheet
marks.text: Under the title, which names the property. Rows and columns are numbered as Excel numbers them, so you can find each one in the file.

marks.label: The verdict
marks.text: How many of the reader’s checks fail (or “every check passes”), then whether the AI agrees.
Closes the window without saving, like **Keep it waiting**.

marks.label: Income · Expenses · NOI
marks.text: The accounts added up, against the totals the statement prints: ✓ when they match, ✗ in red when they don’t.

marks.label: What to look at
marks.text: Every failed check (red) and every point where the AI reads it differently (amber), with its row. Click a row number to jump to it.

marks.label: The rows
marks.text: Every row of the file and what the reader made of it (next picture).

marks.label: Keep it waiting
marks.text: Closes the window. The T12 waits, unused, in Documents, Underwriting and Data Health.

marks.label: Save this reading
marks.text: Saves the reading with your changes; its figures are used everywhere.

views.title: How each row was read
views.text: One line per row of the file. The file’s own name column comes first, then what the reader made of the row. The months and the total, as in the file, are further right: scroll the table sideways.

marks.label: Row
marks.text: The row number in Excel.

marks.label: What the reader made of it
marks.text: Account, Category name, Total, Income total, Expense total, Net Operating Income, Not operating, or Above the header, Header row, Empty.

marks.label: Side
marks.text: Income or Expense (accounts only).

marks.label: Category (in the file)
marks.text: The category the account sits under in the file itself.

marks.label: Underwriting line
marks.text: The line of the Underwriting table it adds to, with the item it is (e.g. “the vacancy”) under it.

marks.label: Amount used
marks.text: The amount the reader takes (grey). Type another to use yours; it then needs a note.

marks.label: Your note
marks.text: Why you changed this row. Kept with the reading and in the property’s change history.

marks.label: Check
marks.text: ✓ = its months add up to its total. A failed check is in red; a row the AI reads differently, in amber, with “AI: …”.

sections.title: Files with several parts
sections.text: A workbook with several properties’ statements asks which part is whose before it is saved. Afterwards the file’s row says “This property’s part: …” with **Change**, or, for a file still waiting, “It has N parts — which one is this property’s?” with **Answer**. See [Split a file that covers several properties](split-a-multi-property-file).

views.title: Which part is whose?
views.text: A made-up workbook with three sheets, added on Sample Elms’ page.

marks.label: The file
marks.text: How many parts and sheets, and which parts are already set to this property.

marks.label: Part 1
marks.text: Sheet 1 of 3 · its sheet name · the property name in it; under it, what it is (T12) and its NOI.

marks.label: Ticked
marks.text: This part will be linked.

marks.label: This property
marks.text: Set to Sample Elms: its name matches. Each list offers Don’t link, this property, every other property, and “Add as a new property” named after the part.

marks.label: Another property
marks.text: Part 2 names Sample Oaks: it goes to Sample Oaks’ folder.

marks.label: Not linked
marks.text: Maple Court is no property in the app: not ticked, “Don’t link”.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Nothing is saved.

marks.label: Approve
marks.text: Saves the file to each property, with its own part.

sections.title: A T12 that names no property

views.text: A T12 added on a property’s page whose sheet doesn’t name that property.

marks.label: Which sheet is …’s T12?
marks.text: The property you are on.

marks.label: Why it asks
marks.text: The file doesn’t name this property.

marks.label: A sheet
marks.text: Use this sheet as the property’s T12; it then goes through the T12 check.

marks.label: None — keep it as a document
marks.text: Saved as an “Other” document; no figure is taken from it.

marks.label: Save it
marks.text: Saves the file with your answer.

views.text: Opened by **Pages & properties** on a PDF’s row. Split the PDF into parts by pages, or give a part to several properties: each property reads only its own pages.

marks.label: Which pages belong to which property?
marks.text: The file and how many pages it has.

marks.label: Pages … to …
marks.text: The part’s first and last page.

marks.label: What it is
marks.text: An optional name for the part (e.g. Loan agreement, Phase 1).
Removes the part.

marks.label: Property
marks.text: The property this part belongs to.

marks.label: + another property
marks.text: The same pages go to a second property too.

marks.label: + Add a part (pages)
marks.text: Another page range, for another property.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Nothing changes.

marks.label: Approve
marks.text: Saves the parts; the file is copied to each property named.

sections.title: When Claude isn’t connected
sections.text: Without Claude, a new T12 can’t be checked against a second reading, so the app asks what to do. Here a made-up T12 added while Claude is signed out.

marks.label: Claude isn’t connected
marks.text: “The AI couldn’t read this T12” when Claude is connected but its reading failed.

marks.label: The file
marks.text: Which property and file, and that it hasn’t been checked. Nothing from it is used yet.

marks.label: The reader’s checks
marks.text: Whether the app’s own reader passes every check.

marks.label: Keep it waiting
marks.text: Kept, unused, until you review it, or Claude is back and you read it again.

marks.label: Use the reader’s reading
marks.text: Shown only when every check passes: the T12 is used as the reader read it.

marks.label: Review it myself
marks.text: Opens the review window.

views.title: Used as the reader read it

marks.label: T12: Read by the reader only (Claude wasn’t connected)
marks.text: In use without Claude’s check. Once Claude is connected, **Read again** in Underwriting checks it with Claude.

pages.title: The calendar
pages.description: Every part of the Maturity & Reset Calendar tab: the decision box, the tiles, the maturity wall, the events, the month view and the tool bar.
pages.intro: Each picture names its controls. Point at a number, on the picture or in the list, to find it.

views.text: The calendar is built from every active loan in the book (an archived property, a removed or paid-off loan is left out) and is redrawn whenever a loan changes. Your view and filters stay as you left them while the tab is open.

marks.label: Portfolio
marks.text: Back to the portfolio. The calendar tab stays open.

marks.label: Calendar
marks.text: This tab.

marks.label: Pop out
marks.text: Opens the calendar in a window of its own, handy on a second screen. Clicking an event there still opens the loan here.

marks.label: Close tab
marks.text: Closes the calendar. Nothing is lost: it is rebuilt from the loans next time.

marks.label: Maturity & Reset Calendar
marks.text: The title, and the day it was built (today).

marks.label: The tool bar
marks.text: List or Calendar, the filters, Sort, Clear and Print.

marks.label: Needs a maturity decision
marks.text: Loans that have matured or whose extension is undecided, always on top.

marks.label: The four tiles
marks.text: The totals at a glance; each tile is also a filter.

marks.label: Maturity wall
marks.text: How much debt comes due each year.

views.text: A red box on top lists every loan whose status is **Matured** (set by hand, or by itself once the maturity date has passed) or **Extension undecided** (set by hand in the loan’s edit form, **Loan Status**). It stays, even after the date has passed, until you change the status (**Extended**, **Paid off**…).

marks.label: Needs a maturity decision (2)
marks.text: How many loans wait for a decision.

marks.label: Extension undecided
marks.text: An extension is being discussed and not yet settled.

marks.label: Matured
marks.text: The loan has reached its maturity (or you marked it so) and is not extended or paid off yet.

marks.label: The loan
marks.text: Click the row to open that loan’s page.

marks.label: Date · balloon
marks.text: Its maturity date, and the balloon: what is left to pay then.

sections.title: The tiles and the maturity wall

views.title: The four tiles
views.text: Four totals over the loans the filters let through. Click a tile to list exactly the loans it counts; click it again to show everything.

marks.label: Debt maturing (shown)
marks.text: The balloons of every maturity in the calendar added up, and how many there are.

marks.label: Maturing (next 12 mo)
marks.text: Loans whose maturity falls within the next 12 months.

marks.label: ARM resets (next 12 mo)
marks.text: Adjustable-rate loans whose rate (and payment) changes within 12 months.

marks.label: IO step-ups (next 12 mo)
marks.text: Loans whose interest-only period ends within 12 months: the payment steps up to principal and interest.

views.title: A tile as a filter
views.text: A clicked tile filters the list (and switches to the List view).

marks.label: The tile you clicked
marks.text: Outlined while it filters the list.

marks.label: Showing …
marks.text: What the list shows now. Click here, or the tile again, to show everything.

marks.label: Only those loans
marks.text: The rows are exactly the ones the tile counts.

views.title: Maturity wall
views.text: Debt coming due by year: one bar per year, as long as that year’s balloons.

marks.label: The year
marks.text: Each year with at least one maturity.

marks.label: A red bar
marks.text: Coming due this year or next: the closest refinancings.

marks.label: A green bar
marks.text: A later year. The longest bar is the year with the most debt maturing.

marks.label: The amount
marks.text: The total of that year’s balloons.

views.text: Every event in date order, grouped by year. Click any row to open that loan at the event’s payment.

marks.label: Date
marks.text: The day of the event: the maturity date, the payment date the new rate starts, or the first full payment after interest-only.

marks.label: Event
marks.text: Maturity (red), ARM reset (amber) or IO ends (green).

marks.label: Loan
marks.text: The loan.

marks.label: Amount
marks.text: The balloon for a maturity; the balance at that date for a reset or an IO step-up.

marks.label: Detail
marks.text: In words: the balloon due, the new rate and payment, or the new P&I payment.

marks.label: Year
marks.text: Where each year’s events start.

marks.label: Within 12 months
marks.text: A yellow row is less than a year away.

marks.label: The kind of event
marks.text: Maturity, ARM reset or IO ends.

marks.label: Needs a decision
marks.text: A pink row: the loan matured or its extension is undecided. Its status is shown next to the event.

marks.label: An event
marks.text: Click it: the app goes to Portfolio, opens this loan and jumps to that payment in its schedule.

views.text: Click **Calendar** in the tool bar: one box per year, and the first year with events open. Each event is a small card in its month, edged in its color.

marks.label: List
marks.text: Back to the list view.

marks.label: Calendar
marks.text: This view.

marks.label: The colors
marks.text: Red = maturity, amber = ARM reset, green = interest-only ends.

marks.label: A year
marks.text: The year, how many events and how much matures. Click it to close or open its months.

marks.label: A month
marks.text: The month’s events. An empty month shows “—”.

marks.label: An event
marks.text: The loan, the kind of event and the amount. Point at it to read the detail; click it to open the loan.

views.title: Open another year
views.text: Click a closed year’s line to open its twelve months; click an open one to close it. Several years can be open at once.

marks.label: A closed year
marks.text: ▸ = closed. Click to open it.

marks.label: An open year
marks.text: ▾ = open: its twelve months are below.

marks.label: Needs a decision
marks.text: A loan that matured, or whose extension is undecided, is edged in red (or amber) with a warning line.

marks.label: An event
marks.text: Click it to open the loan.

views.title: Lender
views.text: Every lender in the book. Tick one or more to show only their loans.

marks.label: Lender
marks.text: Opens and closes this list.

marks.label: Every lender
marks.text: Tick a lender to show only its loans; tick several to show all of theirs.

marks.label: A tick box
marks.text: On = this lender’s loans are shown.

views.title: A lender ticked
views.text: The tiles, the wall and the list count only that lender’s loans. Untick it, or click **Clear**, to see everything again.

marks.label: Lender (1)
marks.text: One lender is ticked.

marks.label: The tiles
marks.text: Now only that lender’s loans.

marks.label: The wall
marks.text: Only that lender’s maturities.

views.title: Loans
views.text: Pick loans by name. Type in the search box to shorten the list, then tick the loans to show.

marks.label: Loans
marks.text: Opens and closes this list.

marks.label: Search loans
marks.text: Type part of a name; only the loans that match stay in the list.

marks.label: The loans
marks.text: Tick a loan to show only it; tick several to show them together.

marks.text: The smallest amount shown (here 50m = $50,000,000).

marks.label: Amount — max
marks.text: The largest amount shown. Blank = no limit.

marks.label: Sort
marks.text: Date, Smallest amount or Largest amount.

marks.label: Date
marks.text: By date, earliest first, grouped by year (the usual order).

marks.label: Smallest amount
marks.text: Smallest amount first.

marks.label: Largest amount
marks.text: Largest amount first.

views.text: **Clear** removes every filter (lenders, loans, amounts, the search and the tile you clicked); the view and the sort stay. **Print** opens your computer’s print window with the calendar as you see it now, without the tool bar.

marks.label: Clear
marks.text: Removes every filter.

marks.label: Print
marks.text: Prints the calendar, or saves it as a PDF from the print window.

marks.label: Back to blank
marks.text: No filter is on after Clear.

marks.label: Sort stays
marks.text: Clear doesn’t change the order. Set Sort back to Date yourself.

pages.title: Data Health
pages.description: Every part of the Data Health tab: the lists of what needs you, the four numbers, the table of every property, and Recompute.
pages.intro: Each picture names its controls. Point at a number, on the picture or in the list, to find it.

views.text: On top, what needs you: the T12s waiting for review, files waiting for an answer and files without a property (each list only when it has something in it, or a green line when it is clear). Then four numbers, whether every property has its folder, possible duplicates and maturity decisions. The table of every property is at the bottom.

marks.label: Data Health
marks.text: This tab. Pop it out or close it like any tab.

marks.label: Data Health
marks.text: The version of the app that is running is named under the title.

marks.label: Recompute all figures
marks.text: Works out every property’s figures again from its files (see “Recompute” below).

marks.label: Last recompute
marks.text: When the figures were last worked out, for how many properties, and why (by hand, after an update…).

marks.label: T12s that need your review
marks.text: T12s waiting for you before they are used.

marks.label: Files with several parts
marks.text: Workbooks waiting for you to say which part is whose.

marks.label: Files without a property
marks.text: Folders no property uses any more.

marks.label: Properties
marks.text: How many properties, and how many active loans.

marks.label: With a T12
marks.text: How many have a T12 in use; the rest are “missing”.

marks.label: Units known
marks.text: How many have their number of units set in the profile; the rest are blank.

marks.label: Need a maturity decision
marks.text: Loans that matured or whose extension is undecided.

marks.label: Properties without a folder
marks.text: Always 0: every property has its folder with its profile and general data. Anything else names the property the app couldn’t make a folder for.

views.title: The list
views.text: Every T12 waiting for you, with the property, the file and why. Green and “0” when there is nothing to review. A T12 read by an older version that passes every check but hasn’t been read by the AI yet is counted on a grey line under the list; it is checked as soon as Claude is connected.

marks.label: T12s that need your review
marks.text: How many wait for you.

marks.label: A T12 waiting
marks.text: The property · the file — why it waits (here the AI disagrees on 2 points). Its numbers are not used yet.

marks.label: Review
marks.text: Opens the reading, row by row, to decide.

marks.text: Reads every saved T12 again with the reader and the AI. It shows “Re-checking… 1 of 5” while it works; a T12 that now fails or disagrees is listed here.

views.title: Review
views.text: The T12 reading: every row of the file and what the reader made of it, the checks, and where the AI disagrees. See [Check a T12](check-a-t12).

marks.label: The verdict
marks.text: Whether every check passes, and whether the AI agrees with the reader.

marks.label: Income, Expenses, NOI
marks.text: The accounts added up, against the totals the statement prints (✓ when they match).

marks.label: What to look at
marks.text: Each failed check and each point the AI reads differently, with its Excel row. Click the row number to jump to it.

marks.label: The rows

views.text: Every file with several parts whose part for a property isn’t answered yet. A file filed before this was asked, matched by its name only, is listed under “Matched by name only — confirm once”, with a **Confirm** button.

marks.label: Files with several parts waiting
marks.text: How many files wait for an answer.

marks.label: Answer
marks.text: Opens the question.

views.title: Which part is whose?
views.text: Each part of the file is a line: tick it and pick the property it belongs to. A part can go to any property, several parts to one property (they are added together), or one part to several. Nothing is saved until you approve.

marks.label: Which part of this file belongs to which property?
marks.text: The file, how many parts and sheets, and the property it is asked for.

marks.label: A part

marks.label: Tick box

marks.label: Property
marks.text: Don’t link, this property, any other property, or “Add as a new property” named after the part.

marks.label: Cancel

marks.text: Links each ticked part to its property. Each property reads only its own parts, never another’s numbers.

views.text: Tick a part without picking its property and click **Approve**: a red line says which part still needs one. Pick the property, or untick the part.

marks.label: Ticked
marks.text: This part is ticked…

marks.label: …but no property
marks.text: …and its property is still “Don’t link”.

marks.label: Pick a property for part 1 — or untick it.
marks.text: What is missing. Nothing was saved.

marks.label: Files without a property
marks.text: How many folders belong to no property.

marks.label: The old name
marks.text: The property name the files were saved under.

marks.label: Its files
marks.text: How many, and the first few names.

marks.label: attach to
marks.text: The property to move them to.

marks.label: Attach
marks.text: Moves the files into that property’s folder (asks first).

marks.label: Delete
marks.text: Deletes the files (asks first).

views.title: Attach — the question
views.text: The files move into the chosen property’s folder; a file with the same name there is kept as a copy, never replaced.

marks.label: Attach these files to …?
marks.text: The property you picked.

marks.label: What happens
marks.text: Where the files go.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Nothing is moved.

marks.label: Attach
marks.text: Moves them; the list is drawn again without that folder.

views.title: Delete — the question
views.text: The files belong to no property, so deleting them changes no figure; the automatic backups still keep a copy.

marks.label: Delete the files of …?
marks.text: The old name.

marks.label: What happens
marks.text: It can’t be undone here; the automatic backups keep a copy.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Nothing is deleted.

marks.label: Delete
marks.text: Deletes the folder; the list is drawn again.

views.title: The list
views.text: Two properties that may be one building entered twice: the same street address and city or, when one has no address, nearly the same name (ignoring capitals, punctuation and words like “The” or “Apartments”). They are never merged by themselves.

marks.label: Possible duplicate properties
marks.text: How many pairs.

marks.label: The pair
marks.text: The two property names.

marks.label: Why
marks.text: Same street address and city, or similar names when one or both have no address.

marks.label: Not a duplicate
marks.text: Remembers that these two are different buildings: the pair is not shown again (here or in Settings).

views.title: After “Not a duplicate”
views.text: The pair is gone. With no pair left, a green line says how many distinct properties and loans there are.

marks.label: No duplicate properties detected
marks.text: Every property is distinct (the pairs you marked are left out).

marks.label: Properties
marks.text: Both stay as two properties: nothing was merged.

views.text: Loans that matured, or whose extension is undecided: set in the loan’s edit form (**Loan Status**), or **Matured** by itself once the maturity date has passed. A loan leaves the list when you change its status (**Extended**, **Paid off**…). The Maturity & Reset Calendar shows the same loans on top.

marks.label: Loans needing a maturity decision
marks.text: How many.

marks.label: Extension undecided
marks.text: An extension is being discussed and not settled.

marks.label: Matured
marks.text: Past (or marked at) its maturity, not extended or paid off yet.

views.title: The columns
views.text: One row per property, with what the app knows about it. Properties missing a T12 or units come first.

marks.label: Property
marks.text: Its name (how many loans if more than one) and whether its profile is complete, or what it still needs.

marks.label: Status
marks.text: Worked out from its data: Stabilized, No T12 yet, No loan data yet or Third-party managed.

marks.label: T12 / NOI basis
marks.text: How the NOI is taken from the T12 (12-month total, last 3 months × 4…) and how many months of history.

marks.label: Units
marks.text: From the property’s profile.

marks.label: In-place NOI
marks.text: The NOI the app uses for it.

marks.label: Computed
marks.text: When its figures were last worked out, and by which app version (red when an older version).

marks.label: Warnings
marks.text: no T12, units unknown, NOI ≤ 0, loan matured, extension undecided, figures from an older version, or “ok”.

marks.label: Open
marks.text: Opens Underwriting for that property.

views.title: Warnings on a row
views.text: A row with a maturity decision pending, another whose loan has matured, and a made-up property with no loan yet. A property whose figures were worked out by an older version of the app shows “figures from v…” and a red version under **Computed**; Recompute fixes that.

marks.label: extension undecided
marks.text: One of its loans waits for a maturity decision.

marks.label: no T12
marks.text: No T12 in use yet: add one in its Documents or in Underwriting.

marks.label: units unknown
marks.text: Its number of units isn’t set in its profile.

marks.label: In-place NOI —
marks.text: No NOI yet: it comes from the T12.

marks.label: loan matured
marks.text: A loan of this property has matured.

marks.label: No loan data yet
marks.text: A property with no loan (here the made-up “Queens Gate”).

marks.label: Profile
marks.text: “Profile complete”, or what its profile still needs (address, units…).

marks.label: Open
marks.text: Opens Underwriting for this property.

views.title: Open
views.text: **Open** takes you to Underwriting with that property picked, ready for its T12 and figures.

marks.label: Underwriting
marks.text: Opened (or brought forward) by Open.

marks.label: Property
marks.text: The property whose Open you clicked.

marks.label: Waiting for your review
marks.text: Its T12 still waits; Review opens the same window as in Data Health.

views.text: Every figure from a T12 is kept with the property and worked out again when the app is updated. **Recompute all figures** does it now: the button reads “Recomputing…” while every property’s figures are worked out again from its saved files, then the page is drawn again. Use it after changing files outside the app, or when the **Computed** column shows an older version.

marks.label: Recompute all figures
marks.text: Works everything out again.

marks.label: Last recompute … · manual
marks.text: When, how many of the properties, and the reason (manual = this button).

pages.title: The assistant window
pages.description: Every control in the assistant window: the buttons on top, the chat, the property and model pickers, the message box, the Approve card, History and the connection.
pages.intro: Opened by **Assistant** at the bottom right of every tab. Each picture names its controls. Point at a number, on the picture or in the list, to find it.

views.text: The window takes about 80% of the app window; the app stays as it was underneath (see [Ask the assistant](ask-the-assistant#ask-a-question)). A new chat starts with a few example questions.

marks.label: Compact
marks.text: Shortens a long chat into a summary that keeps the facts, so Claude stays quick. Your messages stay saved.

marks.label: New chat
marks.text: Starts a fresh conversation. The current one is kept in History; nothing in your loans changes.

marks.label: History
marks.text: Your saved conversations: open, search, rename, pin or delete them.

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Closes the window (so does clicking outside it). The chat stays as it is for next time.

marks.label: Connection
marks.text: Green: Claude is connected and ready. Amber: it isn’t (see “Connection” below).

marks.label: Example question
marks.text: Click one to ask it straight away.

marks.label: Property
marks.text: Points the chat at one property, or keeps it general. Claude reads that property’s saved files first, and files you attach are saved to it.

marks.label: Model
marks.text: Which Claude model answers. “Automatic” lets your subscription choose; the others are the models it offers.

marks.label: Effort
marks.text: How hard Claude thinks: Low is fastest, Max reasons the deepest (a little slower). High is the default.

marks.label: Attach
marks.text: Adds files to the message: PDF, Word, Excel, text or pictures. They are read on your computer.

marks.label: Message
marks.text: Your question, or what you want done. Enter sends; Shift+Enter starts a new line.

marks.label: Send
marks.text: Sends the message. While Claude works, it turns into Stop.

marks.label: Connection settings
marks.text: How the app connects to Claude: your Claude subscription or an API key.

marks.label: Your message
marks.text: What you asked, on the right.

marks.label: Claude’s answer
marks.text: On the left. Worked out from the app’s own figures; it never makes up a number, and says so when something is missing.

marks.label: Follow-up
marks.text: Ask the next question here; the conversation carries on.

views.title: Attached files
views.text: Files attached to a message show above the message box.

marks.label: Attach
marks.text: Opens your computer’s file window to pick one or more files.

marks.label: Attached
marks.text: The files going with your message, and how much was read from each. The × on a file removes it.

marks.label: Saved files
marks.text: How many files are already saved with this property. When you send, the attached file is saved to it too.

marks.label: Message
marks.text: Say what you want done with the file.

views.text: Every change Claude proposes waits on a card like this one. Nothing changes until you approve it.

marks.label: The card
marks.text: What Claude wants to do, line by line.

marks.label: Tick box
marks.text: Only ticked lines are applied; untick one to leave it out.

marks.label: Old → new
marks.text: The value now (crossed out; “none” when empty) and the value Claude proposes.

marks.label: Where it came from
marks.text: The file, page and quote the value was read from, so you can check it.

marks.label: Approve & apply
marks.text: Makes the change, saved in the field’s history as “Assistant, approved by You”.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Nothing is changed; Claude is told you said no.

marks.label: Stop
marks.text: Claude is waiting for your answer. Stop ends its turn and cancels the card; nothing is changed.

views.title: After you approve
views.text: A card is used once. Cards that wait for you are never applied by themselves.

marks.label: Done
marks.text: The card is closed: it says what was applied (✓) and what was left out. Its buttons are greyed.

marks.label: Claude’s report
marks.text: Claude is told exactly what happened, and says so.

views.text: Every saved chat, grouped by property: the property you’re on first, then the portfolio, then the rest. Point at a chat for its buttons.

marks.label: Search
marks.text: Finds words in every saved chat.

marks.label: This property / All
marks.text: Only this property’s chats, or all of them.

marks.label: Back to chat
marks.text: Returns to the conversation you were in.

marks.label: Group
marks.text: The property (or Portfolio) the chats below belong to.

marks.label: A chat
marks.text: Its title (your first question), how many messages and when. Click it to reopen it and carry on.

marks.label: Pin, Rename, Delete
marks.text: Shown while the pointer is on the chat. The star (Pin) keeps it at the top; the pencil (Rename) gives it your own title; the bin (Delete) deletes the conversation (it asks first).

views.title: Connection settings
views.text: **Connection settings**, under the paperclip, opens the Claude connection window: how the app connects to Claude. Signed in to your Claude subscription, nothing else is needed. The same window opens from **Settings**. See [Connect Claude](connect-claude).

marks.label: Status
marks.text: Green: connected, and how. Amber: not connected, and what is missing.

marks.label: Sign out
marks.text: Signs this computer out of your Claude subscription. The assistant stops until you connect again.

marks.label: Advanced — API key
marks.text: Opens the API-key choice, for pay-as-you-go use instead of a subscription.

marks.label: Anthropic API key
marks.text: Paste a key from console.anthropic.com. It is kept only on this computer and never shown again.

marks.label: Save
marks.text: Saves the key and switches the app to use it.

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Closes this window.

views.title: When Claude isn’t connected
views.text: The status turns amber, **Send** is greyed out, and the connection choices open inside the chat by themselves.

marks.label: Not connected
marks.text: What is missing, in plain words.

marks.label: Connect with your Claude subscription
marks.text: Opens a small sign-in window that takes you to your browser. When you finish, the status turns green.

marks.label: Automatic
marks.text: Uses your Claude subscription, and an API key if one is saved (recommended).

marks.label: Claude subscription
marks.text: Only the subscription: no API key, no per-use billing.

marks.label: Anthropic API key
marks.text: Only an API key: pay as you go.

marks.label: API key
marks.text: Paste a key here. It is kept only on this computer and never shown again.

marks.label: Save
marks.text: Saves the key; the status checks again.

marks.label: Send (greyed)
marks.text: Waits until Claude is connected, so a message is never lost.

pages.title: The Settings and Data menus
pages.description: Every control in Settings and in the Data menu, the guide window, the Claude connection and the version chip.
pages.intro: Settings is in the window bar at the top right, on every tab. The Data menu is under the tabs, on the right. Each picture names its controls. Point at a number, on the picture or in the list, to find it.

views.text: Five parts, top to bottom. Click outside the menu, or press Esc, to close it.

marks.label: Settings
marks.text: Opens and closes this menu.

marks.label: Display
marks.text: App scale: makes the whole app bigger or smaller.

marks.label: Portfolio targets
marks.text: The DSCR, LTV and debt-yield targets the Portfolio page measures against.

marks.label: Portfolio
marks.text: How many properties there are, each one by name, and any that look like duplicates.

marks.label: Open the guide
marks.text: Opens this guide (see below).

marks.label: Cloud
marks.text: The Claude connection for the AI features.

views.title: App scale
views.text: Everything below the window bar grows or shrinks at once, like zoom in a web browser. The window bar keeps its size, so Settings is always easy to reach. The app starts at 100% each time you open it.

marks.label: Size now
marks.text: The size the app is at.

marks.label: Slider
marks.text: From 50% to 200%, in steps of 5%.
Half size: the most fits on the screen.
Normal size (lit when it is the size now).
Double size. 75%, 125% and 150% are in between.

marks.label: Reset to 100%
marks.text: Back to the normal size.

views.title: Portfolio targets
views.text: What the Portfolio page measures against: its tiles, the Coverage vs targets chart and the coverage table (clears / off target). Type a figure and click away, or press Tab. See [Set the portfolio targets](set-portfolio-targets).

marks.label: Minimum DSCR
marks.text: NOI ÷ yearly loan payments should be at least this (1.25× to start).

marks.label: Maximum LTV
marks.text: Balance ÷ value should be at most this (75% to start).

marks.label: Minimum debt yield
marks.text: NOI ÷ balance should be at least this (8% to start).

marks.label: Where they are used
marks.text: Only on the Portfolio page. The refinance’s “Can you?” limits are fixed; Underwriting sets its sizing limits for each property.

views.title: Your properties
views.text: How many properties the app counts, each one listed by name, so you can check the count against your own list. Below the list, any two properties that may be one building: the same street address, or similar names where one has no address. Here two made-up properties, “Sample Court” and “Sample Court East”, are flagged.

marks.label: Properties
marks.text: How many properties there are; under it, how many loans they hold.

marks.label: Every property
marks.text: Numbered, with the start of each one’s address. Scroll it to see them all.

marks.label: Possible duplicate
marks.text: The two names, and why they were flagged.

marks.label: Not a duplicate
marks.text: They really are two buildings: the pair isn’t flagged again.

marks.label: If they are one building
marks.text: Rename one to match the other (on its property page) and they become one property.

views.title: After “Not a duplicate”
views.text: The app remembers the pair. Data Health shows the same check.

marks.label: No duplicates
marks.text: Nothing left to look at.

sections.title: The guide
sections.text: **Open the guide** in Settings opens this guide in a window over the app, on its Overview. Esc or **×** closes it.

views.title: A page
views.text: The pages are on the left, in groups. A how-to page gets one task done, step by step; a reference page names every control on a screen.

marks.label: Guide
marks.text: Back to the Overview.

marks.label: Search the guide
marks.text: Finds every page, section and step with all the words you type. Ctrl K jumps here.

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Closes the guide (so does Esc).

marks.label: The pages
marks.text: Every page, in its group. The page you are reading is lit.

marks.label: The page
marks.text: Its title, what it gets done, and what you need first.

marks.label: On this page
marks.text: The page’s sections. Click one to jump to it; the one you are reading is lit.

views.title: Steps and pictures
views.text: Each step is one action. A picture shows the app where the screen changes, with numbers on what the step points at. At the foot of each page, **Next steps** and **Previous** / **Next** lead on.

marks.label: A step
marks.text: What to do, and what happens then.

marks.label: The picture
marks.text: The app itself. Click it to see it full size; click again, or press Esc, to go back.

marks.label: A number
marks.text: Point at it, or at its line in the list, and both light up with the part of the screen it marks.

marks.label: What each number is
marks.text: The same numbers, in words. With more than three, the list sits beside the picture on a wide window.

views.title: Search
views.text: Every page, section and step that has all the words you typed, with where it is. Click one to go there; Enter opens the first.

marks.label: Search
marks.text: What you typed.

marks.label: Results
marks.text: How many places match.

marks.label: A result
marks.text: Its group, page and section, and its first words. Click to go there.

sections.title: Claude connection
sections.text: Opened by **Claude connection** at the foot of Settings. See [Connect Claude](connect-claude).

views.title: Connected
views.text: The top line says whether the app can reach Claude, and how. Here it is signed in with a Claude subscription. Close the window with **×** or by clicking outside it.

marks.label: Claude connection
marks.text: Your Claude subscription or an API key.

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Closes the window.

marks.label: State
marks.text: Green: connected, and how. Amber: not connected, and what to do.

marks.label: Sign out
marks.text: Disconnects your Claude subscription on this computer.

marks.label: Advanced
marks.text: Use an Anthropic API key instead.

views.title: Advanced — an API key
views.text: For pay-as-you-go use at console.anthropic.com instead of a subscription. Once a key is saved, **Clear** appears beside **Save** and removes it.

marks.label: Advanced
marks.text: Opens and closes this part.

marks.label: Anthropic API key
marks.text: Paste the key here (it starts sk-ant-). It is hidden as you type.

marks.label: Save
marks.text: Saves the key and switches the app to use it.

marks.label: Where it is kept
marks.text: Only on this computer.

views.title: Not connected
views.text: Before you connect, or after **Sign out**. The line at the top turns amber and says what is missing.

marks.label: Not connected
marks.text: Says what is missing.

marks.label: Connect with your Claude subscription
marks.text: Opens a small sign-in window that takes you to your browser.

marks.label: How it works
marks.text: What happens when you click it.

sections.title: The Data menu
sections.text: The **Data** button is under the tabs, on the right, on both sides of the **Whole Portfolio** / **Specific Property** switch.

views.text: Backups of everything, and loans in and out of Excel. Below them, the backups the app takes by itself.

marks.label: Data
marks.text: Opens and closes this menu.

marks.label: Back up to a file…
marks.text: Saves everything to one file you choose: every loan, every property’s folder (profile, assumptions, T12s, documents), every chat and your settings.

marks.label: Restore from a file…
marks.text: Replaces everything with a backup file you pick. It asks first, and saves what you have as an automatic backup.

marks.label: Export all loans to Excel…
marks.text: A workbook of every active loan.

marks.label: Import loans from Excel…
marks.text: Adds or updates loans from a workbook.

marks.label: An automatic backup
marks.text: Why it was taken (“After: Added property …”, “After a change”, “Before Excel import”, “Before a restore”), when, and what it holds. Click to restore it.

marks.label: Open folder
marks.text: Opens the folder with the automatic backups on your computer.

views.title: Restoring a backup
views.text: Before a restore, the app says exactly what the backup holds and what it replaces. **Restore** replaces your loans, property folders and chats, then the app reloads with the restored data.

marks.label: Restore …?
marks.text: What the backup holds.

marks.label: What happens
marks.text: What is replaced, and that your current data is saved first, as a “Before a restore” backup.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Nothing changes.

marks.label: Restore
marks.text: Restores the backup.

views.text: Exactly what the workbook will hold: one column per active loan, one row per field, in sections. The values can’t be edited here. Removed, paid-off and archived loans aren’t exported.

marks.label: Export to Excel
marks.text: A preview of the workbook.

marks.label: How many
marks.text: How many loans will be exported.

marks.label: Field
marks.text: Each row is one field of a loan, grouped in sections (the green bands).

marks.label: A loan
marks.text: Untick to leave this loan out.

marks.label: Select all
marks.text: Ticks or unticks every loan.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Closes without exporting.

marks.label: Export
marks.text: Saves the workbook (your computer’s Save window opens).

views.title: Before you import
views.text: The details every loan in your sheet needs. Loans can be in rows or in columns, and small differences in the headers are fine; an export from the app always works.

marks.label: Before you import
marks.text: What your sheet needs.

marks.label: The details
marks.text: Every detail a loan needs.

marks.label: I’ve checked
marks.text: Tick it to turn on Choose file…

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Closes without importing.

marks.label: Choose file…
marks.text: Opens your computer’s Open window to pick the workbook.

views.title: Review import
views.text: Nothing has changed yet. Each loan in the workbook is a row with its status, and you can edit any cell. This made-up workbook holds an export of two sample loans (one with a changed insurance escrow) and two made-up loans, one of them incomplete.

marks.label: Review import
marks.text: What the workbook would do.

marks.label: Counts
marks.text: New, updated, unchanged, and how many need attention.

marks.label: unchanged
marks.text: Matches a loan you have; nothing differs.

marks.label: update
marks.text: Matches a loan you have; the changed details will be written to it (only the details the sheet has).

marks.label: new
marks.text: No match: it will be added.

marks.label: missing data
marks.text: Needs a detail the sheet didn’t have.

marks.label: + Add loan
marks.text: Adds an empty row to fill in.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Closes; nothing is imported.

marks.label: Resolve 1 to import
marks.text: Turns into **Apply import** once nothing needs attention. Apply saves an automatic backup first.

views.text: At the right of the header, under the window bar. See [Update the app](update-the-app).

marks.label: Property count
marks.text: How many properties are in the portfolio.

marks.label: Version
marks.text: Your version. Click to check for an update: “Checking for updates…”, then “Update available…” and “Downloading update… %”. Green “Update ready — Restart” means one is downloaded; click it to restart into it.

pages.title: The shared database screens
pages.description: The sign-in window, the menu under your name, the bar for unsaved changes, the admin’s and the maintainer’s screens, offline and view only.
pages.intro: With the shared database your team works on one copy of the loans, properties and files: you sign in, every change is saved with a reason, and the group’s admin decides who can change what. Each picture names its controls. Every person, email address and group in the pictures is made up.

sections.title: Signing in
sections.text: With a shared database, the app opens on its sign-in window. See [Sign in or create an account](sign-in).

marks.label: Email
marks.text: The email address of your account.

marks.label: Password
marks.text: Your password.

marks.label: Sign in
marks.text: Opens the app on your group’s loans, properties and files.

marks.label: Create an account
marks.text: For someone new: asks to join your company’s group.

marks.label: Forgot your password?
marks.text: Emails you a code to set a new password.

marks.label: Minimize
marks.text: Hides the window to the taskbar.

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Closes the app.

marks.label: Email
marks.text: The email of the account whose password you forgot.

marks.label: Email me a code
marks.text: Sends a 6-digit code. The window then asks for it.

marks.label: Back to sign in
marks.text: Returns to the sign-in window.

marks.label: Sent
marks.text: The code is on its way (it only goes to an email that has an account).

marks.label: The code
marks.text: The 6 digits from the email.

marks.label: New password
marks.text: At least 8 characters.

marks.label: Again
marks.text: The same new password, to be sure it’s typed right.

marks.label: Set the password and sign in
marks.text: Saves the new password and opens your group’s data.

marks.label: Organization
marks.text: Type the first 3 letters of its name.

marks.label: Pick yours
marks.text: The groups whose name starts with those letters. Click yours; only these can be joined.

marks.label: Full name
marks.text: Your name, as the admin and the change history will show it.

marks.label: Email
marks.text: Your work email. The admin sees it, and the confirmation goes there.

marks.label: Password
marks.text: At least 8 characters.

marks.label: Again
marks.text: The same password again.

marks.label: Sign up
marks.text: Sends your request to join to the group’s admin.

marks.label: I have an account
marks.text: Back to the sign-in window.

views.title: Waiting for approval
views.text: After **Sign up** the request goes to the group’s admin, in the app and by email. When they approve it, you get an email: confirm your address from it, then sign in.

marks.label: What happens now
marks.text: “Waiting for approval”. (Someone the admin already added is told to confirm their email instead.)

marks.label: Who approves
marks.text: The group and its admin, and the next steps.

marks.label: Back to sign in
marks.text: The sign-in window, with your email filled in.

views.title: Signing in before approval
views.text: Until the admin approves, the sign-in window reminds you of your request, and signing in says the account isn’t ready yet.

marks.label: Your request
marks.text: Which group you asked to join, and what to do once approved.

marks.label: Not ready yet
marks.text: Why signing in didn’t work yet.

views.text: An account that isn’t in a group yet (say, its admin removed it) can ask to join from here.

marks.label: Not in a group
marks.text: You’re signed in, but no group has you yet.

marks.label: Signed in as
marks.text: The account you’re signed in with, and what to do.

marks.label: Organization
marks.text: Type the first 3 letters of its name …

marks.label: Pick it
marks.text: … and click it.

marks.label: Full name
marks.text: Your name for the admin.

marks.label: Ask to join
marks.text: Sends the request to the group’s admin.

marks.label: Check again
marks.text: Once the admin approves, this opens the group.

marks.label: Sign out
marks.text: Back to the sign-in window.

sections.title: The maintainer
sections.text: The maintainer looks after the shared database for every company. Each company is a group with one admin; the maintainer makes the groups and names their admins.

marks.label: The maintainer
marks.text: Signed in as the maintainer, in no group of their own.

marks.label: Ask to join a group
marks.text: A maintainer can also ask to join a group, like anyone in no group.

marks.label: A group
marks.text: Each group, its admin (“hasn’t signed in yet” until they do) and how many people it has.

marks.label: New admin…
marks.text: Makes someone else the group’s admin. The old admin stays in the group as an editor.

marks.label: New group
marks.text: The company’s name.

marks.label: Its admin’s email
marks.text: The person who will run the group.

marks.label: Admin’s name
marks.text: Their full name.

marks.label: Create
marks.text: Makes the group. Its admin then creates an account (**Create an account**, then the group’s name) and needs no approval, only to confirm the email.

marks.label: Check again
marks.text: Opens the group, once the maintainer is in one.

marks.label: Sign out
marks.text: Back to the sign-in window.

views.title: Groups, from the menu
views.text: A maintainer who is also in a group has **Groups** in the menu under their name.

marks.label: A group
marks.text: The group, its admin and how many people.

marks.label: New admin…
marks.text: Makes someone else its admin; the old admin stays as an editor.

marks.label: New group
marks.text: The company’s name.

marks.label: Its admin’s email
marks.text: Who will run it.

marks.label: Admin’s full name
marks.text: Their name.

marks.label: Create
marks.text: Makes the group. Its admin then creates an account and only confirms the email.

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Closes the screen.

views.text: The admin’s app shows people waiting to join as soon as it opens (they also got an email). **Asking to join** in the menu opens it again.

marks.label: Who asks
marks.text: Their name, email and when they asked.

marks.label: Turn down
marks.text: They get an email saying so.

marks.label: Approve
marks.text: They get an email to confirm their address, then join as an editor. (Make them view only in Members and codes.)

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Decide later: the request waits.

views.text: Click your name in the window bar. An admin sees every screen; an editor or a viewer sees only the change history and **Sign out**.

marks.label: The chip
marks.text: Name · role; “offline”, how many changes wait for you and how many people ask to join, when there are.

marks.label: The group
marks.text: The group, you, your role, and online (live) or offline (the last picture of the data).

marks.label: Requests
marks.text: Changes members asked you to approve.

marks.label: Asking to join
marks.text: People who asked to join.

marks.label: Members and codes
marks.text: Who is in the group and who can edit; your approval and offline codes.

marks.label: Daily backups
marks.text: Put the group’s data back as it was on a day.

marks.label: Start the group over…
marks.text: Removes all the group’s data, to upload the starting data again (asks you to type the group’s name). Before the first upload this is “Upload this computer’s data”.

marks.label: Change history
marks.text: Every change: who, when, why.

marks.label: Groups
marks.text: Only the maintainer: every group and its admin.

marks.label: Sign out
marks.text: Back to the sign-in window. Changes not saved yet are dropped (it asks first).

sections.title: Saving a change
sections.text: See [Save a change](save-a-change).

views.title: Not saved yet
views.text: **Not saved yet**: any change you make is only on this computer, in this bar, until you say why and save it.

marks.label: What changed
marks.text: The changes waiting (point at it for the full list).

marks.label: Why
marks.text: Required. Kept in the change history with your name.

marks.label: Save
marks.text: Saves for everyone in the group (so does Enter).

marks.label: Undo
marks.text: Drops your changes; the data goes back to how it was.

views.title: A member’s change waits for the admin
views.text: A member who changes what the admin changed needs the admin’s approval. Their request pops up in the admin’s app.

marks.label: Who and when
marks.text: The member who asked, and when.

marks.label: The change
marks.text: What, its value now, and their change.

marks.label: Turn down
marks.text: Asks for an optional note for them; nothing changes.

marks.label: Approve
marks.text: Their change takes effect for everyone.

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Decide later (menu › **Requests**).

views.text: The admin’s screen: who is in the group and what each person can do. People join by asking from the sign-in window. See [Manage members and codes](manage-members).

marks.label: The admin
marks.text: The group’s one admin.

marks.label: Can
marks.text: Editor (can change data) or View only. It takes effect in their app at once.

marks.label: Remove
marks.text: Takes them out of the group (it asks first). Their app says so.

marks.label: Not signed in yet
marks.text: Approved, but hasn’t confirmed the email and signed in yet.

marks.label: Approval code
marks.text: Typed on a member’s screen to approve on the spot a change to what you changed.

marks.label: Offline code
marks.text: Lets you keep changing data on your own computer with no connection.

marks.label: Save the codes
marks.text: At least 6 characters each; an empty box keeps that code as it is.

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Closes the screen.

views.text: Every change to the group’s data, newest first. Type in the box to find a name, a property or a reason.

marks.label: Find
marks.text: Shows only the changes with these words.

marks.label: When
marks.text: Date and time of the change.

marks.label: Who
marks.text: Who made it, and who approved it for a member’s change the admin approved. “The app” for the app’s own work.

marks.label: Approved by
marks.text: A member’s change the admin approved names them both.

marks.label: What
marks.text: The property or loan, and the field.

marks.label: Before
marks.text: The value before.

marks.label: After
marks.text: The value after.

marks.label: Why
marks.text: The reason typed when it was saved.

marks.label: Older changes
marks.text: Loads the next 200 older changes.

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Closes the screen.

sections.title: Daily backups
sections.text: The admin’s screen. A backup of the group’s data is taken every day and kept 30 days.

marks.label: Put this day back
marks.text: The group’s data goes back to how it was that day, for everyone (it asks why first).

marks.label: Empty
marks.text: Taken before the group had data: nothing to put back.

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Closes the screen.

views.title: Putting a day back
views.text: Every change it makes is in the change history, with your reason.

marks.label: Why
marks.text: Required; kept in the change history.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Nothing changes.

marks.label: Put it back
marks.text: Puts the day back for everyone.

sections.title: Offline
sections.text: With no connection, the app keeps the last picture of the group’s data, view only. It reconnects by itself.

views.title: Offline: view only
views.text: A banner says so and the chip turns amber. You can look at everything; changes can’t be saved until the connection is back.

marks.label: Offline
marks.text: The chip says “offline” (amber dot).

marks.label: The banner
marks.text: What offline means: the last picture of the data, view only.

marks.label: Use my offline code
marks.text: Only the admin: keep changing data while offline.

views.title: The offline code
views.text: The admin types the offline code (set in Members and codes). Changes are kept on this computer, each with its reason, and go up when the connection is back.

marks.label: Offline code
marks.text: The code you set in Members and codes.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Stay view only.

marks.label: Unlock
marks.text: You can change data offline; the banner says how many changes wait to go up.

sections.title: As an editor
sections.text: What a member who isn’t the admin sees. Here Eddie is an editor.

views.title: The admin’s approval is needed
views.text: An editor changes what the admin changed: **Save** asks for the admin’s approval. The admin can type the approval code right there, or the editor sends it to them.

marks.label: The change
marks.text: What, its value now, and the change.

marks.label: Approval code
marks.text: The admin types their code here (on the editor’s screen) to approve it now.

marks.label: Undo my change
marks.text: Drops it.

marks.label: Send to the admin
marks.text: It pops up in the admin’s app. The current value stays until they approve; you get a note when they decide.

marks.label: Approve with the code
marks.text: Saves at once with the admin’s code.

views.title: The editor’s menu
views.text: A member’s menu has the change history and **Sign out**.

marks.label: Editor
marks.text: Eddie · Editor.

marks.label: The group
marks.text: The group, who you are and your role, online or offline.

marks.label: Change history
marks.text: Every change: who, when, why.

marks.label: Sign out
marks.text: Back to the sign-in window.

views.text: Someone the admin made view only sees everything in the group but can’t change it: a change they try is refused, and the screen goes back.

marks.label: View only
marks.text: Vera · View only.

marks.label: The banner
marks.text: View only: you can see everything in the group but not change it.
